Give another user access to your contacts

If you use Workspace, you can give other users in your domain permission to access and manage your contacts. These delegates can add and update your contacts with information like names, phone numbers, and addresses.

Your contacts delegates now have more management options. If you had delegates prior to the latest update they might have lost access if you did not reapprove them. However, you can always re-invite them.

Important: Access to your contacts doesn’t grant access to your email account.

Requirements

  • Your Directory administrator must turn on contact sharing. If you’re an admin, learn how to turn the global Directory on or off.
  • You can delegate contacts only to people in the same domain or org as you.
  • You and your delegates must be signed in to your accounts with your work or school.
  • You and your delegates must be on a computer, not a phone or tablet.

Delegate your contacts

  1. Navigate to Google Contacts.
    • Make sure that you’re signed in with your work or school account.
  2. At the top right, click Settings Delegate access.
  3. Click Invite delegate.
  4. Enter the name or email address of the person you want to give permission to manage your contacts.
    • Tip: You can enter up to 25 names, separated by commas.
  5. Click Send.

The users you invite can now access your Contacts.

Tip: Users can’t view and edit delegated contacts with the Contacts app from a mobile device.

About what delegates can and can’t do

Delegates can:

  • Find personal information from your profile, regardless of the visibility settings for those profile fields. This includes your:
    • Gender
    • Birthday
    • Email addresses
    • Phone numbers
    • Tip: Find the complete list in your Google Account.
  • Add new contacts with the “Create contact” or “New contact” buttons.
  • Edit or delete contacts in the delegated contacts list.
  • Search for contacts in the search bar.
  • Undo changes.
  • Add, edit, and delete labels for contacts in the delegated contacts list.
  • Manage Other contacts.

Delegates can’t:

  • Import contacts.
  • Export or forward contacts.
  • Find and merge duplicates.
  • Change the settings or preferences.
  • Find and delete contacts from trash.

Manage contacts delegated to you

If someone in your organization gives you access to their contacts, you can manage their contacts from your account.

  1. Navigate tolinkGoogle Contacts.
    • Make sure that you’re signed into your work or school account.
  2. On the left menu, select the name of a person who delegated their contacts to you.
    • You can now manage their contacts.
  3. Contacts you add or edit when you manage their contacts will appear in their contacts, not yours.

You can now:

  • Add, edit, and delete their contacts.
  • Search within their contacts with the search bar.
  • If you search for a delegated contact with the same email or name as a directory contact, the autocomplete result returns the directory contact.
  • (Available as of November 2023) Add, edit, and delete labels for their contacts.
  • (Available as of November 2023) Manage their Other contacts.

To switch between people who have delegated their contacts to you, select the delegator’s name. You can only review and manage contacts for the person you’ve selected.

Search contacts delegated to you

If you have many contacts delegated to you, you might need to search the list of contacts to quickly find a contact. To search delegated contacts:

  1. Navigate to Google Contacts.
    • Make sure that you’re signed into your work or school account.
  2. At the top left, click Menu Delegated contacts, and click the name of the person who delegated their contacts to you.
  3. In the search box at the top, enter the name or email of the contact you want to search for and press Enter.

Tip: If you search for a delegated contact who has the same email or name as a directory contact, the autocomplete result returns the directory contact.

Save contact info when you interact with people

I get a Contacts error

You may have issues with Google Contacts. You may receive an error message, or may not be able to access Contacts. Check the fixes below for these issues.

“Gmail is temporarily unable to access your contacts”

Try again in a few minutes while we work to fix the problem.

While we fix it, you can still email people in Gmail when you type their full email address.

“Can’t update contact”

If you get this error, you might have exceeded your Contacts storage quota. This means you might have saved too many contacts, or too much info for one contact.

You can save up to 25,000 contacts or 20 MB with photos not included.

For each contact, you can save up to:
  • 128 KB
  • 1,024 characters per field (except “Notes”)
  • 500 fields total
You can also:
  • Delete contacts from your Trash.
  • Export & back up contacts, then delete the contacts you don’t need.
  • Merge duplicate contacts.
  • Cut words from contact fields.

Contacts service is not available

If you do not have access to Google Contacts, the Contacts service will need to be turned on for your work, school, or other group domain. Ask your domain admin to turn on Contacts by signing in to their Google Workspace control panel, finding Contacts, and clicking the “Add” button.

Import your contacts into Google Contacts

You can import your contacts into Google Contacts from other sources.

Import from an existing CSV or vCard file

  1. On your computer, go to Google Contacts.

  2. On the left, click Import Select file.

    1. If you don’t find the menu on the left, at the top left click Menu .
    2. For CSV files, look for the .csv file extension. For vCard files, look for the .vcf file extension.

  3. Choose your file.

  4. Click Import.

Tip: If you can’t find a detail about a contact you imported once the import has finished, check the notes section for that contact.

Use a template spreadsheet to create a CSV file to import

You can use a template to make sure your contacts’ details are imported into the right fields in Google Contacts.

Step 1: Fill out the contacts template

Important: Do not delete the header row in the template. These headings help make sure your contacts’ info is saved to the right place in Google Contacts.

  1. Open the sample template.
  2. Click Make a copy.
    • If you want to download the template to another application, like Excel:
      1. Click File Download.
      2. Choose the application where you’d like it saved.
      3. Open the spreadsheet in that application.
        • If your cells are merged or formatted incorrectly in the opened file, check that application’s support channels.
    • If the option to make a copy doesn’t appear, click menu Make a copy.
      1. If “Make a copy” is not an option, select Share & export Make a copy.
  3. Fill in the spreadsheet with the details for all contacts you want to import.
    • You can fill in the columns that you want to save to Google Contacts and delete the columns you don’t use.
    • A new contact is created for every row that has any entered data.
  4. Click File Download Comma Separated Values (.csv).
  5. Save your file.
    • Make sure to save it someplace you’ll remember, like your desktop.

Tip: If you’re not familiar with Google Sheets, learn more about how to use it.

Step 2: Upload your file to Google Contacts
  1. Open Google Contacts.
  2. On the left, click Import .
    • If you don’t find the menu on the left, at the top left click Menu .
  3. Click Select file Select your new contacts file.
  4. Click Import.
    • When the import is done, Google Contacts will open your newly imported contacts.

Find descriptions for all template column headers and fields

To make sure your contacts’ info imports exactly where you want it to, use the headers from the template. You can learn about the template’s headers and how contact fields are formatted.

  • Header name: Name Prefix; Field description: Prefix for your contact. For example: “Dr” or “Prof.”
  • Header name: First Name; Field description: First or given name for your contact.
  • Header name: Middle Name; Field description: Middle or additional name for your contact.
  • Header name: Last Name; Field description: Last or family name for your contact.
  • Header name: Name Suffix; Field description: Suffix for your contact. For example: “Sr” or “Jr.”
  • Header name: Phonetic First Name; Field description: Phonetic pronunciation for your contact’s first or given name.
  • Header name: Phonetic Middle Name; Field description: Phonetic pronunciation for your contact’s middle or additional name.
  • Header name: Phonetic Last Name; Field description: Phonetic pronunciation for your contact’s last or family name.
  • Header name: Nickname; Field description: Nickname for your contact.
  • Header name: File as; Field description: Name used to organize your contact.

Contact fields:

  • Header name: Email - Label; Field description: Label of the email. For example: “Home” or “Work.”
  • Header name: Email - Value; Field description: Email for your contact. For example: “contact@gmail.com.”
  • Header name: Phone - Label; Field description: Label of the phone number. For example: “Home” or “Work.”
  • Header name: Phone - Value; Field description: Phone number for your contact. Use a “+” to indicate a country code. For example: “+1 234 567 8901.” Spaces, dashes, and parenthesis are optional.

Address fields:

  • Header name: Address - Label; Field description: Label of the address. For example: “Home” or “Work.”
  • Header name: Address - Country; Field description: The country of the address.
  • Header name: Address - Street; Field description: The street of the address.
  • Header name: Address - Extended Address; Field description: The secondary street of the address if it has one.
  • Header name: Address - City; Field description: The city of the address.
  • Header name: Address - Region; Field description: The state, province, prefecture, and more of the address.
  • Header name: Address - Postal Code; Field description: The postal code of the address.
  • Header name: Address - PO Box; Field description: The post office box of the address.

Organization fields:

  • Header name: Organization Name; Field description: The name of the contact’s organization, like a company or school.
  • Header name: Organization Title; Field description: The contact’s title in their organization.
  • Header name: Organization Department; Field description: The contact’s department in their organization.

Event fields:

  • Header name: Birthday; Field description: Birthday for your contact. Can be formatted as either YYYY-MM-DD or –MM-DD if there’s no year.
  • Header name: Event - Label; Field description: Label of the event. For example: “Anniversary.”
  • Header name: Event - Value; Field description: Date for this contact’s event. Can be formatted as either YYYY-MM-DD or –MM-DD if there’s no year.

Other fields:

  • Header name: Relation - Label; Field description: Label of the relation. For example: “Spouse” or “Cousin.”
  • Header name: Relation - Value; Field description: Name of the relation. For example: “Alice Jones” or “Bob.”
  • Header name: Website - Label; Field description: Label of the website. For example: “Profile” or “Blog.”
  • Header name: Website - Value; Field description: Website address.
  • Header name: Custom Field - Label; Field description: Label for the custom field. Useful if you’d like to save contact data that doesn’t fit in one of the default fields offered above.
  • Header name: Custom Field - Value; Field description: Value for the custom field.
  • Header name: Notes; Field description: Notes on your contact. Any text can be entered here.
  • Header name: Labels; Field description: Names of the labels this contact is a part of. You can enter multiple values here separated by “:::”. For example: “Work Friends ::: Family ::: Project11.”

Tip: If you have contacts with multiple emails, phone numbers, and more, you can insert extra columns in the template to enter this data.

From a Google Account

Step 1: Export existing Google contacts
  1. On your computer, go to Google Contacts.
  2. At the top right, click Export .
  3. Select which contacts to export.
  4. Click Google CSV Export.
  5. Save the file someplace you’ll be able to find it easily.
  6. At the top right, click your profile picture Sign out.
Step 2: Import the file
  1. On your computer, go to Google Contacts.
  2. Sign in with your other Gmail Account.
  3. On the left, click Import Select File.
  4. Choose your file.
  5. Click Import.

Learn how to fix import problems

You can have problems when:

  • You import more than 3,000 contacts at a time. If you have more than 3,000 contacts, split them into multiple CSVs before you import them.
  • You reach the limit of 25,000 contacts.Learn about contact size limits.
  • The contacts aren’t formatted to work with Google Contacts. Make sure to save your contacts as a vCard or CSV file.

Merge duplicate contacts

If you have duplicate listings for the same person in Google Contacts, you can merge them.

You can’t merge contacts that are saved in different Google Accounts.

  1. Go to Google Contacts.
  2. At the top left, click Menu Merge & fix.
  3. If you don’t find a “Merge duplicates” option, you don’t have any contacts that you can merge. If you find contacts that you can merge:
    • To accept one or more duplicate contact suggestions, click Merge.
    • To accept all duplicate contact suggestions, click Merge all.
  4. Optional: If you want to choose which contacts to merge:
    • Go to Google Contacts.
    • To select the contacts you want to merge, hover over each profile picture or monogram. Then, check the box.
    • At the top right, click .

Separate merged contacts

You can separate a contact that you merged.

Learn how to undo changes to contacts.

Review & share your contact info

You can keep your contact info updated on your Android phone and share your details directly from your phone. Before you share your contact info, review it to make sure it is correct. If you need to edit it, learn how to change your Google Account picture and name.

To check your info:

  1. On your Android device, open the Contacts app .
  2. Tap Your info.
    1. If you’re not logged into the Contacts app, tap Organize Settings Your info.
  3. Review your details:
    1. Your Google Account name, picture, and email for the account selected in the Contacts app.
    2. Phone number(s) from your device’s SIM card(s).
  4. To add custom contact info, like an additional phone number or address, tap Edit, enter more information, and tap Save.
    1. Custom contact info will only appear in the Contacts app and Phone app on your Android device. It will not be added to your Google Account info.
  5. To select a default phone number or email to use when you share your contact info, long-press on the phone number or email, and tap Set default.

Tip: If you change your Google Account name or picture, it sometimes takes a few days to update across all Google products.

Share your own contact info

Important: When you share your own info from the Contacts app, the recipient will receive a VCF file.

To share your own contact info right from your Android phone:

  1. Open the Contacts app .
  2. Tap Your info Share.

Tips:

  • Account changes: If you share your Google Account name or picture and change it later, people you shared with may still see the old info in their contact record for you.
  • Google services info: If you choose not to share your Google Account name or picture, this info might still show up to people you contact or share with on Google services.

Sync Google Contacts with your mobile device or computer

You can sync your Google Contacts to a phone, tablet, and computer. When you change a contact, that contact will change everywhere.

If you’re new to iPhone, learn how to sync Google Contacts to your phone.

On a Mac computer

  1. On your Mac computer, open System Preferences.
  2. Click Internet Accounts.
  3. Click Google. Note: To use a different account, in the bottom left, click Add Google.
  4. Enter your email address and password. Click Next.
  5. Check Contacts.
  6. Click Done.

On a Windows 10 computer

  1. On your Windows computer, open Settings.
  2. Click Accounts ** Email & App Accounts** Add an Account Google.
  3. Enter your email address and password.
  4. Review the permissions, then click Allow.
  5. Click Done.

Use Google Contacts with a screen reader

You can use a screen reader with Google Contacts.

Screen readers you can use

  • Operating system: Microsoft Windows; Screen reader: NVDA or JAWS; Browser: Firefox
  • Operating system: Mac; Screen reader: VoiceOver; Browser: Safari
  • Operating system: Chrome OS; Screen reader: ChromeVox; Browser: Google Chrome

Keyboard shortcuts

For the following shortcuts to work, your screen reader should be switched to “Focus mode” for NVDA or “Forms mode” for JAWS. If you use VoiceOver or Chromevox, you don’t need to use any special modes.

  • Action: Move to Search box; Shortcut: /
  • Action: Open list of keyboard shortcuts; Shortcut: ?
  • Action: Go to next contact; Shortcut: j or →
  • Action: Go to previous contact; Shortcut: k or ←
  • Action: Select current contact; Shortcut: x
  • Action: Select all contacts in a list; Shortcut: a
  • Action: Open contact details; Shortcut: Enter
  • Action: Save edits to a contact; Shortcut: ⌘ or Ctrl + Enter
  • Action: Undo last action; Shortcut: z

Navigate Google Contacts

Google Contacts includes 5 main sections:

  • Google bar
  • Search box
  • Navigation list
  • List of contacts
  • Contact details

Google bar

The Google bar provides links and pop-up menus related to your Google Account, like other Google applications, account notifications, and the link to sign out of your account.

Links & menus in the Google bar
  • Apps: Opens to let you navigate to other Google applications.
  • Unread notifications: Shows notifications from your Google+ account. If you use Google+ and you have Google+ notifications, you can read them here.
  • Account: Lets you sign out, add an account, manage your account, or see Google’s privacy policy. If you use Google+, the menu also has a link to your Google+ profile.

Search

To move focus to the Search box, where you can search your contacts, press /.

Navigation list

The navigation list controls which contacts appear in the main view, and it includes links to other tools and resources.

Options in the navigation list
  • All contacts
  • Frequent: Frequently contacted contacts
  • Duplicates: Review and merge duplicate contacts in your account
  • Labels: Organize your contacts into groups
  • More: Explore other options, like Import, Export, and Print
  • Settings
  • Help & feedback

Contacts list and details

The main contacts view includes a list of your contacts.

To view or edit the details for a contact, press Enter.

To return to the contacts list, press Escape.

View, group & share contacts

You can organize the people and businesses in Contacts using labels.

You can use the Contacts app to find someone’s contact info or organize contacts with labels like “friends” or “family.”

Create a group

  1. Go to Google Contacts.
  2. On the left next to “Labels,” click Create label .
  3. Type a name, then click Save.

Add or remove contacts from a group

Add contacts to a group

  1. Go to Google Contacts.
  2. Select one of the following:
    • A single contact: Check the box next to the contact name.
    • Multiple contacts: Check the boxes next to all the contacts you want to add.
    • All contacts: Check the box next to any contact and in the top left, click Selection Actions All.
  3. At the top, click Manage labels .
  4. Click the group label you want.
  5. Click Apply.

Tip: If a contact has multiple email addresses, only their default email address is added to the label group. You can use the Contacts app on an Android device to change the default email address for a contact.

Remove contacts from a group

  1. Go to Google Contacts.
  2. At the left, click a group name.
  3. Select contacts to remove by checking the boxes that show up next to their names.
  4. At the top right, click Label .
  5. Uncheck the group name.

Edit or delete a group

  1. Go to Google Contacts.
  2. At the left, under “Labels,” point to the group you want to edit or delete.
  3. Follow the steps on the screen.

Use groups in Gmail

Email a group

  1. Open Gmail.
  2. At the top left, click Compose.
  3. In the “To” field, start typing the group name, then select the group from the list that appears.
  4. You’ll see a list of contacts in the “To” field.

Create or edit groups

Note: If you use Gmail for work or school and someone gives you access to their Gmail, you can manage labels on their contacts, too.

  1. Open Gmail.
  2. At the top left, click Compose.
  3. Click To, Cc, or Bcc.
  4. Find a contact, then check the box next to their name.
  5. Click Manage labels.
  6. Change or add group labels:
    • To add the contact to a group label, click the group label, then click Apply.
    • To remove the contact from a group label, click the group label, then click Apply.
    • To create and add a new label, click Create label. Then follow the onscreen steps.

Ask questions about a PDF with Gemini

Important: This feature is only available for:

  • Gemini Advanced users. Learn how to upgrade to Gemini Advanced.
  • Devices with Android 15 or later versions.

To ask questions and find info about a PDF file, you can use Gemini in Files by Google:

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. Open a PDF file.
    • Learn how to search for a file.
  3. While you view a PDF, use Gemini on your Files by Google app.
    • Press and hold the Power button.
    • Or, say “Hey Google.”
  4. Tap Ask about PDF.
    • When you include a PDF file with your prompt, Gemini analyzes it to provide information in a response. Learn more about how Google uses uploaded files.
    • You can only add PDFs that are less than 25 MB in size.
    • Protected PDFs aren’t supported.
  5. Enter your question.
    • Or, to speak, tap Microphone .
  6. Tap Send .
  7. To continue your conversation with Gemini and expand the window, tap Open in New .

Compress your files

You can use Files by Google to compress files to save storage space or if you need files in zip format.

What you need

To compress files with Files by Google, you need Android 8 version or up.

Compress your files

Important: Files will be compressed to zip format.

To compress your files into a zip file:

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. Select the files or folders you want to compress.
  3. Next to the files or folders you want to compress, tap More .
  4. From the dropdown menu, tap Compress.
  5. Name the zip file.
    • Make sure your zip file name doesn’t include spaces or periods. The compressed file will have a .zip extension.

How to scan documents with Files by Google

You can quickly scan documents in Files by Google and save them as searchable PDFs.

Scan documents with the Files app

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. At the bottom right, tap Scan .
  3. Point your device’s camera at the document you want to scan.
    • A blue outline indicates where the picture will be cropped.
  4. Take a photo of the document that you’d like to scan.
    • To enable automatic capture, you can either select Auto capture or Manual.
  5. When you preview your scanned document, you can:
    • Adjust scan area: Tap Crop and rotate .
    • Adjust the colors or make the image greyscale: Tap Filter .
    • Remove unwanted objects: Tap Clean .
    • Scan multiple documents at once: Tap Add .
    • Retake the photo: Tap Retake .
    • Delete a page: Tap Delete .
  6. Once the scan is complete, tap Done.
  7. You can find your scanned doc under “Recents” on the app homepage, or find them in the Scanned folder.

Tip: Scanned documents are automatically saved as PDFs.

Find your scanned documents

You can find your scanned documents in a dedicated “Scanned” folder in the “Downloads” directory.

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. Tap Documents Scanned.

Tip: If you can’t find your scanned PDF files, you can also type 0 in your search bar.

Manage permissions

Files by Google requires the following permissions:

  • Location: Allows the app to find your friends nearby using Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
  • Device call management: Allows read-only access to your phone including the status of any ongoing calls and current cellular network information to make sure your carrier supports a local Wi-Fi hotspot, which is used for high-speed file transfer.
  • Storage: Allows Files by Google to access your device’s storage so the app can manage files.
  • SD card write permissions: Allows you to rename, delete, move, copy files to your SD card.

Manage your Starred files

To easily access frequently used files, you can mark them as Starred.

Important: If you uninstall and reinstall the app, you need to mark your files as Starred again.

  2. Select a category or a storage device.
  3. Find the files you want to mark as Starred.
    • To mark one file:

        2. At the top right, tap More Add to Starred.
      • In List view :
        1. Next to the file, tap More Add to Starred.
    • To mark multiple files:
      • In Grid view :
        1. Press and hold a file.
        2. To select more files, at the top of each file, tap the circle.
        3. At the top right, tap More Add to Starred.
      • In List view :
        1. Next to a file, tap More Select.
        2. To select more files, next to each file, tap the circle.
        3. At the top right, tap More Add to Starred.
  4. At the bottom, you’ll find a confirmation message “Added to Starred.”
  5. Files that are marked as Starred are represented with Star .

Open, manage & edit PDFs in Files by Google

You can directly open and edit PDF files in the Files by Google app.

Open & manage a PDF

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. Under “Recents,” you can find your recently added or downloaded PDF files, or search for a PDF file.
  3. Tap the PDF file you want to open. From the open PDF, you can take these actions:
    • To zoom in and center a section of the PDF, pinch or double tap on that section of the document.
      • To fit the width to the page, double tap again.
    • To share a PDF, tap Share .
    • To mark a PDF as favorite, tap Star .
    • To do more actions, tap More . You can:
      • Open with: Open the PDF in a different app.
      • Move to Trash: Move a PDF to Trash. Learn how to move files to Trash & restore files from Trash.
      • Move to: Move your PDF to a new location on your device. Learn how to move files to a new folder in Internal storage.
      • Copy to: Copy a PDF to a folder on your device. Learn how to copy files to a new folder in Internal storage.
      • Move to Safe folder: To protect the PDF with a PIN or pattern, move your PDF to Safe folder. Learn how to protect your files with Safe folder.
      • File info: Find the PDF details like the modified time and location of the file. Learn how to view file information.
      • Find in file: Search for specific text in the PDF. To find the next or previous usage of the text, tap Arrow up or Arrow down .
      • Print: Print the opened PDF file.

Tip: To open the previous and next files, swipe left or right.

Edit a PDF with annotations

You can annotate PDFs in Files by Google.

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. Open a PDF.
  3. At the bottom right, tap Edit .
  4. At the bottom, you can find the toolbar with multiple annotating tools. To select an annotating tool, you can use a stylus or your finger.
    • Pen:
      • To annotate or mark over the PDF, use freehand strokes. You can choose the brush size and color.
    • Highlighter:
      • To highlight text, use freehand strokes. You can choose the highlighter size and color.
    • Erase:
      • To erase any individual line that you create, wipe through the line.
    • Undo:
      • Undo any action on the PDF.
    • Redo:
      • Redo any action on the PDF.
    • Show annotations:
      • To show all annotations, select Show annotations .
    • Hide annotations:
      • To hide all annotations, select Hide annotations .
  5. At the top right, tap Save copy Upload.
    • When you save a copy, it’s uploaded to your Google Drive. You can rename the file and select which Google Drive folder to save it in.
    • When you upload the new copy, the original copy remains unmarked and saved on your device.

Protect your files with Safe folder

You can hide files in your Safe folder and control access with a PIN.

Tip: This feature is available for Android 8.0 and up.

Set up your Safe folder

Important: If you forget your PIN or Pattern, you can’t access your files.

  1. On your Android device, open the Files by Google app .
  2. Scroll to “Collections.”
  3. Tap Safe folder.
  4. Tap either PIN or Pattern.
    • If PIN is selected:
      1. Enter your PIN.
      2. Tap Next.
      3. In the “Confirm PIN” screen, re-enter your PIN.
      4. Tap Next.
      5. In the “Remember your PIN” screen, tap Got it.
    • If Pattern is selected:
      1. Draw your pattern.
      2. Tap Next.
      3. In the “Confirm Pattern” screen, re-draw your pattern.
      4. Tap Next.
      5. In the “Remember your pattern” screen, tap Got it.

Move files to your Safe folder

  1. On your Android device, open the Files by Google app .
  2. Find the files you want to move to the Safe folder.
  3. If you’re in grid view :
    1. To move files, touch and hold the files.
    2. At the top, tap More Move to Safe folder.
  4. If you’re in list view :
    • To move one file:
      1. Tap More Move to Safe folder.
    • To move multiple files:
      1. Tap More Select.
      2. Next to each file you want to move, check the circle.
      3. At the top, tap More Move to Safe folder.
  5. Enter the current PIN or Pattern that you set.
    • If PIN is set: In the “Confirm PIN” screen, enter your PIN.
    • If Pattern is set: In the “Draw pattern to move” screen, draw your pattern.

Check files in your Safe folder

  1. On your Android device, open the Files by Google app .
  2. Scroll to “Collections.”
  3. Tap Safe folder.
    • To check your files:
      • If PIN is set: Enter your PIN, tap Next.
      • If Pattern is set: Draw your pattern.

Move files out of your Safe folder

  1. On your Android device, open the Files by Google app .
  2. Scroll to “Collections.”
  3. Tap Safe folder.
  4. Enter your PIN.
  5. Tap Next.
  6. Find the files you want to move out of the folder.
    • To move one file:
      • In Grid view :** **
        1. Press and hold the file.
        2. At the top right, tap More Move out of Safe folder.
      • In List view :
        1. Next to the file, tap More Move out of Safe folder.
    • To move multiple files:
      • In Grid view :
        1. Press and hold a file.
        2. To select more files, at the top of each file, tap the circle.
        3. At the top right, tap More Move out of Safe folder.
      • In List view :
        1. Next to a file, tap More .
        2. To select more files, next to each file, tap the circle.
        3. At the top right, tap More Move out of Safe folder.
  7. The file will be moved back to its original location.
    • If the original location isn’t available, the folder will be recreated.

Tip: Stay in Safe folder until the transfer is complete. If you close Safe folder or open another app before the transfer is complete, the operation will be cancelled and the file will stay in Safe folder.

Change your lock

Important: If you forget your PIN or Pattern, you can’t access your files.

  1. On your Android device, open the Files by Google app .
  2. At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  3. Select Safe folder Change lock.
  4. Enter the current PIN or Pattern that you set.
  5. In the “Choose a lock” screen, tap PIN or Pattern.
    • To set up a PIN:
      1. In the “Set a PIN” screen, enter the new PIN.
      2. Tap Next.
      3. In the “Confirm PIN” screen, re-enter the new PIN.
      4. Tap Next.
      5. In the “Remember your PIN” screen, tap Got it.
    • To set up a pattern:
      1. In the “Draw pattern” screen, draw a pattern.
      2. Tap Next.
      3. In the “Confirm pattern” screen, re-draw the pattern.
      4. Tap Next.
      5. In the “Remember your pattern” screen, tap Got it.

Reset your Safe folder

Important: When you reset your Safe folder, the files in this folder will be permanently lost.

  1. On your Android device, open the Files by Google app .
  2. At the top left, tap Menu Settings .
  3. Select Safe folder Reset your Safe folder.
  4. In the confirmation dialog, tap Reset.

Missing files in Safe folder issue

Safe folder keeps your files secure using Android storage with encryption. On rare occasions, files can become corrupt or get deleted. When this happens, no one can access the content of your files anymore including Files by Google.

To secure access to your files, do not:

  • Clear storage or cache with other apps.
  • Plug in an SD card with Safe folder files from another phone.
  • Copy encrypted safe files from old phone to new phone.

Additional information

  • Installed apps can’t be moved to the Safe folder.
  • You won’t find files in the Safe folder in search results or categories.
  • Files in the Safe folder can’t be opened by any third party apps.
  • The “Share” and “Back up to Google Drive” options aren’t available in the Safe folder.
  • Screenshots of the Safe folder can’t be taken.
  • Files in your Safe folder are protected by a lock, but anyone who gains unauthorized access to your device’s internal storage may be able to access them.

Save files to your SD card

You can save files received using the peer-to-peer sharing feature in the File by Google app directly to your SD card.

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google . Learn how to check your storage space.
  2. At the top left, tap More Settings .
  3. Turn on Save to SD card.
  4. You find a prompt that asks for permissions. Tap Allow.
    • If your internal storage runs out of space when you save a file: You’re prompted to save all incoming files to your SD card instead. Tap Save to SD.
    • If “Save to SD card” is turned on and your SD card runs out of space when you save a file: You’re prompted to save all incoming files to your device instead. Tap Save to internal storage.

Tip: If you remove the SD card mid-transfer, you find a “transfer failed” prompt and the transfer is cancelled.

Troubleshooting: SD card undetected issue

Share your files with Quick Share on Files by Google

You can use Quick Share to send and receive files from devices close to your location.

What you need

  • Some of the steps work only on versions Android 13 and up. Learn how to check your Android version.
  • If you find “Nearby Share” on your device, you can still use “Quick Share,” which was previously called “Nearby Share.”
  • Quick Share is available on Android 6+ devices, Chromebooks, and on selected Windows devices through an App.
  • For a Galaxy device with Android 10 and One UI 2.1 or later, the settings and features can be different. Learn about Quick Share feature on Galaxy devices.

Receive files from nearby devices

Important:

  • If you share files between your own devices with the same Google Account, the device that receives it automatically accepts the transfer.
  • If you share files from the clipboard of your own device, the files are automatically copied when someone receives it.
  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. At the bottom right of the screen, tap Quick Share button.
    • Your device is visible to other devices and ready to receive files.
  3. Wait for a pop up notification that tells you who tries to share and what content they want to share with you.
  4. Select Accept or Decline.

Share files with nearby devices

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. At the bottom right of the screen, tap Quick Share button.
  3. Tap Select files to send.
  4. Select the file you want to share.
    • To select multiple files, touch and hold them.
    • Make sure the device you want to share with is nearby so your device can search for it.
  5. Tap the device you want to share with.
    • If you can’t find the device, make sure it has set up “Who can share with you” and its screen is unlocked.
    • If the device you want to share with isn’t listed, you can also share your file with a QR code. Learn how to use QR code with Quick Share.
  6. To accept your sharing request, wait for the other device.
    • To cancel an in-progress transfer, tap the same device again.

Tips:

  • While the transfer is in progress:
    • You can leave the screen, and the transfer continues.
    • A notification shows in your notification tray when you exit the sending screen. From that notification, you can check the status, cancel, or go back to the transfer screen.
  • To select multiple receivers, tap more than one device.
    • Due to technical constraints, only certain device models support simultaneous sharing.
    • In other cases, the transfer queues and receivers you select later can get the transfer request when previous transfers are completed.

Troubleshoot: SD card undetected issue

If Files by Google doesn’t show your SD card:

  1. On your device, tap Settings.
  2. Tap Device maintenance ** Storage**.
  3. Check if your SD card is recognized.

If the SD card isn’t detected in Settings, remove and re-insert the SD card. Once it’s detected in Settings, follow the steps listed below to format the SD card to portable.

If the SD card is recognized in Settings but not in Files by Google, that SD card might be formatted as internal storage. We recommend that you format your SD card as portable storage.

Android offers 2 ways to format SD cards:

  • Portable storage: When you format an SD card as portable storage:
    • You can load files, like pictures and videos, on the SD card.
    • You can’t install apps on the SD card.
    • You can transfer the SD card between devices.
  • Adoptable storage: When you format an SD card as adoptable storage:
    • You can load files, like pictures and videos, on the SD card.
    • You can install apps on the SD card.
    • You can’t transfer the SD card between devices.
    • The SD card replaces internal storage. A 32 GB SD card replaces 32 GB internal storage. The SD card storage isn’t added to the internal storage.

Important: If you format your SD card, data will be permanently deleted. Before you format the SD card, backup your files.

Format a new SD Card into a Portable SD card

On Nokia

How to format SD card on Nokia

  1. On your Nokia device, open the Settings app.
  2. Select Storage SD card.
  3. To open the SD card with Files, select Just once.
    • If you want to open the SD card with a different app, select from your list of apps.
  4. At the top right, select Menu Storage settings.
  5. To format the SD card, select Format Format SD card.
On Lenovo

How to format SD card on Lenovo

  1. On your Lenovo, open the Settings app.
  2. Select Storage & USB SD card.
  3. To format the SD card, select Format Erase & format.
On Xiaomi

How to format SD card on Xiaomi

  1. On your Xiaomi, open the Settings app.
  2. Select Storage SD card.
  3. To open the SD card, select Files Just once.
  4. At the top right, select Menu Storage settings.
  5. To format the SD card, select Format Format SD card.

Format an Adoptable SD card into a Portable SD card

These instructions are for SD cards that are already formatted as internal storage.

On Motorola & Nokia

How to format SD card on Motorola

  1. On your device, open the Settings app.
  2. Select Storage SD card.
  3. At the top right, select Menu Format as portable.
  4. To format the SD card, select Format.
  5. Once all content is moved to the SD card, select Done.
  6. At the top of the home screen, swipe down the “Notification” menu.
  7. In the Settings notification, select Set-up.
  8. To transfer your files to the portable storage, select Portable storage Done.

Use Quick Share on your Android device

With Quick Share, you can immediately send and receive files from nearby devices.

Important:

  • This feature was previously known as Nearby Share. If you still find Nearby Share on some devices, the feature will still work.
  • For a Galaxy device with Android 10 & One UI 2.1 or later, the settings and features can be different. Learn about Quick Share on Galaxy devices.
  • Quick Share is available on Android 6+ devices, Chromebooks, and on select Windows PCsthrough our Quick Share for Windows App.

Find Quick Share on your Android device

From the Share menu

  1. Open the content that you want to share.
  2. Tap Share Quick Share .

From the Quick Settings

  1. To open Quick Settings, on your device, swipe down.
  2. On the Quick Settings menu, scroll to find the Quick Share tile.
  3. Tap Quick Share .
    • If there’s no Quick Share :
      1. Tap Edit .
      2. Under “Quick Settings,” tap Quick Share .

From the device Settings

  1. Open your device’s Settings app.
  2. In the Settings app’s search bar, enter 0.
  3. On the Quick Share page, tap either Receive or Send.

Send content on your Android device

With Quick Share, you can share content with other nearby devices.

Send content through Quick Share

Important: Make sure the device you want to share with is nearby.

  1. On the Quick Share page, select the content that you want to share.
  2. Tap the device you want to share with.
    • If you can’t find the other device, make sure the other device is in “Receive” mode from the Quick Share page.
  3. Wait for the other device to accept your sharing request.
    • Make sure the screen on the other device is unlocked.
    • To cancel an in-progress transfer, select the same device again.
  4. During the transfer:
    • You can leave the screen and the transfer will continue.
    • You’ll get a notification in your notification tray when you leave the sending screen. You can check the status, cancel, or go back to the transfer screen from the notification.
  5. To select multiple receivers, you can tap more than one device.
    • Due to technical constraints, simultaneous sharing is only supported on selected device models.
    • In other cases, transfers will be queued and receivers you select later will get the transfer request when previous transfers are completed.

Tips:

  • On select devices with Android 13 and above, you can also share content from your clipboard with Quick Share.
  • After you copy something, you get a pop-up confirmation at the bottom of the screen.
    1. Tap Devices .
    2. Select the device you want to share the content with.

Send content through Quick Share’s QR code

If you can’t find the device you want to share with, you can also share content through a QR code.

  1. To generate a QR code, on the Quick Share page, tap Use QR code .
  2. Nearby Android devices can scan the QR code to get connected and receive content.

Send content to an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device

For devices with Quick Share support for AirDrop

To send files to an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device, you can use Quick Share on:

  • Pixel 8a or later.
  • Certain Samsung, Oppo, OnePlus, Vivo, Xiaomi, Honor, Transsion, and Motorola devices.
  1. Ask the iPhone, iPad, or macOS user to open their AirDrop settings.
  2. Select Everyone for 10 minutes.
  3. On your device, open the content you want to share.
  4. Tap Share Quick Share.
  5. Select the iPhone, iPad, or macOS device from the list of nearby devices.
  6. Wait for the recipient to accept through the AirDrop notification on their iPhone, iPad, or macOS device.

For iPhone, iPad, and macOS devices, learn how to receive content on an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device.

Tip: Quick Share cross-platform sharing has built-in security and privacy safeguards and is independently tested. For more details, please refer to our Google Security Blog post.

Important: If your Wi-Fi disconnects, it automatically reconnects after you leave the Quick Share page.

For devices without Quick Share support for AirDrop

You can send content to an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device with a QR code. Your files stay secure with end-to-end encryption and remain available for download for 24 hours on Google servers. For successful transfers, both devices need internet access.

Important:

  • If you don’t use Wi-Fi, data charges may apply. You can manage this in “Use mobile data” under “Quick Share settings.”
  • You can share up to 10 GB of files to an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device every 24 hours.
  • You can share up to 1,000 files in a single share session.
  • You can share files to a maximum of 20 iPhone, iPad, or macOS device receivers at a time.
  1. From the Share menu, Quick Settings, or the Device Settings, open the Quick Share page.
  2. Tap Use QR code.
  3. With the iPhone, iPad, or macOS device, scan the QR code for a secure link to download files in the device’s default web browser.
    • Files you share are end-to-end encrypted and uploaded to Google servers. This doesn’t use storage in your personal Google Drive account.
  4. On the Quick Share webpage, the file transfer automatically begins.
    • When the transfer is done, the iOS user can now save the files to their device.
    • The content is available for download for 24 hours.
    • To cancel the transfer, tap the same device again.

Receive content on your Android device

With Quick Share, you can get content from other nearby devices. Content you receive via Quick Share will be available to view and access from the default Files app on your device > Downloads > Quick Share folder.

Receive content through Quick Share

Important:

  • If you share content between your own devices with the same Google Account, the device that receives the share automatically accepts the transfer.
  • If you share content from the clipboard of your own device, the content is automatically copied when someone receives it.
  • On both devices, be sure to turn on Bluetooth .
  • To receive content from someone else, make sure your screen is unlocked.
  • If you want to receive from an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device and you have a Pixel 9 or later (excluding Pixel 9a), adjust your Quick Share visibility settings to Everyone for 10 minutes or be in Receive mode on the Quick Share page.
    • Important: If your Wifi disconnects, it will automatically reconnect after you leave the Quick Share page.
  1. On the Quick Share page, make sure it’s in “Receive” mode.
    • When your device is in “Receive” mode, it’s visible to anyone nearby when you’re on that screen. To stop making your device visible to anyone nearby, exit “Receive” mode.
  2. Wait for a pop up notification that tells you who’s trying to share and what content they want to share with you.
  3. Tap Accept or Decline.

Receive content through Quick Share’s QR code

Important: On both devices, be sure to turn on Wi-Fi and Bluetooth .

To scan a QR code:

From the camera app
  1. Open your device’s camera app.
  2. With the default photo mode, point at the QR code.
  3. Tap on the URL that appears.

Tip: The support to scan the QR code with the default camera app varies by device models. If this doesn’t work on your device, try the QR code scanner through Quick Settings. Learn how to scan QR codes on camera from Google.

From Quick Settings
  1. Open your device’s Quick Settings.
  2. Find and tap Scan QR code .

Tips:

  • When you scan the QR code on the sending device, your device will automatically connect to the sending device to receive the content.
  • If your device doesn’t have a QR scanner in the Quick Settings, learn how to customize your Quick Settings.

Fix problems sharing content

If you try to share or receive content, but it doesn’t work, try these steps:

  • On both devices, check if Bluetooth is turned on. Learn how to turn on Bluetooth.
  • Bring the devices close together, within 1 foot (30 cm) of each other.
  • Turn Airplane mode on, and then off.
  • Wait until no one else is sharing content with the other device.
  • If the device is on Android 12 or earlier, check if Location is turned on. Learn how to turn on location.
  • Turn your device off, then back on.

Receive content on an iPhone, iPad, or macOS device

For devices with Quick Share support for AirDrop

If you share with a Pixel 9 and later, except Pixel 9a, or certain Samsung, Oppo, OnePlus, Vivo, Xiaomi, Honor, Transsion, and Motorola devices:

  1. On your iPhone, iPad, or macOS device, change your AirDrop visibility to “Everyone for 10 Minutes.”
  2. On the AirDrop notification, tap or click Accept.

For devices without Quick Share support for AirDrop

  1. Connect your device to the internet.
  2. When asked, use your camera app to scan the QR code displayed on the Android device.
  3. Tap the link on your screen to open the Google web page. File sharing starts automatically.
    • The files stay encrypted and available to download for 24 hours.
    • You can cancel the transfer at any time.
    • You can’t share this link with others.

To save your files:

  • To save images to the iOS Photos app and documents to the iOS Files app, select Save or Share.
  • To save files to your browser’s Downloads folder, select Download.
    • Some files may download as a zip file. To open it, select the .zip file.
    • Video files can only be downloaded, not saved, or shared.

Adjust Quick Share visibility settings

  1. Open your device’s Settings app.
  2. In the Settings app’s search bar, enter Quick Share.
  3. Tap Who can share with you.
  4. Select from:
    • Your devices: If your screen is off, your device is still visible to your other devices with the same Google Account.
    • Contacts: While your screen is on and unlocked, your device is visible to your nearby contacts.
    • Everyone for 10 minutes: To protect your privacy, your visibility automatically switches back to your previous selection after 10 minutes.

Manage files on a USB

You can move, copy, delete, and rename files on your USB storage device.

Copy a file

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .

  4. Next to a file you want to copy, tap the Down arrow . If you can’t find the Down arrow next to the files, tap List view .
    • To copy one file: Tap the Down arrow Copy to.
    • To copy multiple files:
      1. ****Tap the Down arrow Select.
      2. Next to each file you want to copy, check the circle.
      3. At the top, tap More Copy to.

  6. Tap Copy here.

Move a file

  1. On your Android device, open Files by Google .
  2. Under “Storage devices,” tap your USB storage device.

  4. Next to a file you want to move, tap the Down arrow . If you can’t find the Down arrow next to the files, tap List view .
    • To move one file: Tap the Down arrow Move to.
    • To move multiple files:
      1. ****Tap the Down arrow Select.
      2. Next to each file you want to move, check the circle.
      3. At the top, tap More Move to.
  5. Choose where you want to move the file.
  6. Tap Move here.

Gboard, the keyboard

About proofread with Gboard

With proofread with Gboard, you can check and correct any typed, pasted, or voice dictated text in your text box for writing errors like typos, grammar, and punctuation.

  • To get started, in the pop-up, tap Continue. If you tap “No thanks” you won’t be able to get correction suggestions.

Eligibility requirements:

  • Pixel 8 or 8 Pro
  • English only
  • United States

Use proofread with Gboard

Use Fix it

Important: If you’re using Fix it for the first time, in the pop-up, tap Continue. You can use Fix it on most apps.

  1. On your device, open the app where you’ll input your text.
  2. Enter your text.
  3. If proofreading errors are found, Fix it will give suggestions. Tap Fix it to apply the corrections to your text.
  4. Optional: To remove the correction, tap Undo.
  5. If more proofreading suggestions are available, tap Fix it More fixes.

On Gboard’s menu bar, you can also proofread your text when you tap Proofread .

Turn off Fix it button

  1. Go to Gboard Settings.
  2. Tap Text correction Spelling and Grammar Proofread.
  3. Turn Proofread off.

Change your keyboard theme, sound, or vibration

You can change how Gboard looks, sounds, and vibrates.

Important: If your device’s vibration settings are turned off, your Gboard’s vibration settings will be overridden.

Important: If your device uses Android 8 (Go edition), some of these steps might not work.

Important:

  • Talk-to-text doesn’t work with all languages.
  • Some of these steps work only on Android 7.0 and up. Learn how to check your Android version.

Change how your keyboard looks

You can change your keyboard theme. To give your Gboard a background, like a photo or a color:

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open the Settings app .
  2. Tap System Languages & input.
  3. Tap Virtual Keyboard Gboard.
  4. Tap Theme.
  5. Pick a theme. Then tap Apply.

Change how your keyboard sounds & vibrates

To pick whether your keyboard makes sounds or vibrations, and how loud or strong they are:

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, install Gboard.
  2. Open the Settings app .
  3. Tap System Languages & input.
  4. Tap Virtual Keyboard Gboard.
  5. Tap Preferences.
  6. Scroll down to “Key press.”
  7. Pick an option. For example:
    • Sound on keypress
    • Volume on keypress
    • Haptic feedback on keypress
    • Vibration strength on keypress

Android iPhone & iPad

Copy & paste sections of text with Gboard

You can use Gboard to paste emails, URLs, phone numbers, numbers, addresses, dates, and times. If you copy a section of text that includes info like an email or phone number, you can choose which part of that text to paste into a new area. For example, you can copy an entire text message with the date, address, and URL for an event, then select and paste only the address to share with a friend to meet you there.

Important: Addresses, dates, and times are only available in certain countries and regions and in certain languages.

Copy a text block & paste part of the text

Important:

  • You can paste dates only if they’re written in numerical format. For example, you can paste dates like “3/12/2021,” but you can’t paste dates like “March 12, 2021.”
  • The clipboard clears your history shortly after you last use it. This doesn’t apply to pinned text.
  1. On your phone or tablet, copy a block of text you want to share.
  2. Open the app where you want to paste the text.
  3. Tap an area where you can enter text.
  4. At the top of the keyboard, swipe through the options.
  5. Tap the information you want to paste.
Send the same information to someone else

You can send information that you previously copied and pasted to someone else.

  1. At the top of the keyboard, tap Clipboard .
  2. Tap the information you want to paste.
    • Tip: Tap Back to go back to the keyboard.
Save the pasted text for later

After you’ve pasted copied information once, you can save your text selections to use again.

  1. On your phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap an area where you can enter text.
  3. At the top of the keyboard, tap Clipboard .
  4. Touch and hold the information you want to save.
  5. Tap Pin.
    • Tip: When you’re ready to share it, your selection can be found in the “Pinned” section of your clipboard.

Fix problems with Gboard

If you have issues or privacy concerns with Gboard, try these steps.

Important: If your device uses Android 8 (Go edition), some of these steps might not work.

Before you start

  • Restart your device: Many apps and processes run in the background, and sometimes they can interfere with Gboard.
    • Rebooting your phone restarts all these processes and can resolve minor malfunctions.
  • Update the Gboard app: Make sure you have the latest version of Gboard from Google Play for Android.
    • Updates frequently include bug fixes, performance enhancements, and compatibility improvements.
Gboard is crashing, freezing, or unresponsive

Clear Gboard app cache & data

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps & notifications or Apps Gboard.
  3. Tap Storage and cache Clear cache.
  4. If the issue persists, tap Clear data or Clear storage.
    • This resets Gboard to its default state.

Force close & relaunch Gboard

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps Gboard Force stop.
  3. Reopen your keyboard.

Reinstall Gboard from Google Play

Important: If Gboard is your only keyboard app, install a secondary one.

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps & notifications Gboard.
  3. To remove the app, tap Uninstall.
  4. Open Play Store.
  5. On the search box enter: 0
  6. Tap Install.

Tip: Restart your phone for a fresh start.

Uninstall Gboard updates

If issues started immediately after a Gboard update, uninstalling updates can revert the app to a more stable version.

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps Gboard.
  3. At the top right, tap More Uninstall updates.
Typing lag or incorrect key presses

Clear Gboard app cache

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps & notifications or Apps Gboard.
  3. Tap Storage and cache Clear cache.
  4. If the issue persists, tap Clear data or Clear storage.
    • This resets Gboard to its default state.

Turn off Personalization

  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. At the top of the keyboard, tap Settings Advanced.
  3. Turn off Personalization.
    • This adapts Gboard to your typing and voice typing usage patterns. This can reduce input lag.

Adjust text correction settings

  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. At the bottom left of your keyboard, touch and hold the comma, then move your finger to access Settings .
  3. Tap Text correction.
  4. If it causes unwanted alterations to your text, turn off Smart compose or Auto-capitalization.
  5. To view predictive text and word suggestions, turn on Show suggestion strip.

Manage multiple languages

For smoother typing, stick to one or two active languages.

Voice input problems

Make sure Voice typing is turned on

To grant Gboard microphone access:

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps or App management Gboard Permissions.
  3. Tap Microphone.
  4. Select Allow only while using the app.

To allow Voice typing functionality:

  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap in the text entry field.
  3. At the top of the keyboard, tap Settings Voice typing.
  4. Turn on Voice typing.
    • For improved responsiveness: Turn on Faster voice typing.
    • For Pixel 6 or newer devices: Turn on Advanced voice typing features.

Clear Gboard app cache

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap Apps & notifications or Apps Gboard.
  3. Tap Storage Clear cache.
  4. If the issue persists, tap Clear data.
    • This resets Gboard to its default state.

Check for pending updates & connectivity

  • After setting up a new Pixel phone, it might take a few hours for necessary updates to download.
  • Make sure your phone is connected to Wi-Fi, restart it, and charge it overnight.

Verify language settings

  • To use the Advanced voice typing features: Your primary Gboard language and device language must be the same.
  • To switch Gboard languages:
    • To switch languages, tap the Globe .
    • To select the desired language under Gboard, touch and hold the Globe .

Restore Gboard

Switch back to Gboard

If Gboard switches to another keyboard, you can switch it back.

  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text.
  3. At the bottom of your keyboard, touch and hold Globe .
  4. Tap Gboard.
Add Gboard back to your keyboard list

When you update Gboard, it could disappear from your keyboard list. To add it back:

  1. On your Android device, go to your Settings app.
  2. Tap System Keyboard On-screen keyboard.
  3. Turn on Gboard.

Remove words & check privacy

Delete saved words

Gboard saves the words you type to help you with spelling, and to predict searches you could be interested in. These words are saved only to your device. You can delete saved words whenever you want.

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text.
  3. At the top of the keyboard, tap Settings .
  4. Tap Dictionary Delete learned words.
  5. To confirm that you want to permanently remove these words, enter the number provided.
  6. Tap Ok.

Keep your info secure

We know that what you type on your Android device is personal, so Gboard keeps your info private.

What Gboard sends to Google
  • Your searches are sent to Google to get search results.
  • Usage statistics are sent to let us know which features are used most often, and to help us improve.
  • If you use Gboard’s talk-to-text feature, your voice is sent to Google for transcription.
What Gboard doesn’t send to Google
  • Anything you type, other than your searches, like passwords or chats with friends.
  • Saved words aren’t sent. You can delete saved words at any time.

How to send feedback to Gboard

If you use an Android device, you can send feedback directly from Gboard or through Android Settings.

Send Quality Bug Report (recommended)

If you experience issues with Gboard, you can submit a bug report to help our team improve.

  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. On the left side of the suggestion strip, tap Menu .
  3. Tap Feedback.
    • For faster access in the future, you can drag this icon to the main toolbar.
  4. A form opens to describe your issue.
    • The field “Quality bug report:” is added at the start.
  5. Enter a detailed description of the bug you experienced.
  6. To submit your report, tap Send.
Send feedback through comma on Gboard
  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. At the bottom left of your keyboard, touch and hold the comma, then move your finger to access Settings .
  3. At the bottom, tap Help & feedback Send feedback.

Android iPhone & iPad

Get word suggestions & fix mistakes

You can use suggestions to type faster.

Availability

The Gboard suggestions feature is available on Pixel 4a and later. This feature offers suggestions to supported languages only, and is available in English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. Learn whether your language is supported.

Get started with Gboard

Important:

  • Talk-to-text doesn’t work with all languages.
  • Some of these steps work only on Android 7.0 and up. Learn how to check your Android version.
  1. On your Android phone or tablet, install Gboard.
  2. Open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  3. Tap where you can enter text.
  4. Type a word. At the top of the keyboard, you’ll see suggestions:
    • If you see the word you want, tap it.
    • If you don’t like a suggested word, touch and hold it, and then drag the word to Trash .

Use proofread with Gboard

Important: At this time, proofread with Gboard is only available in the US in English.

With proofread with Gboard, you can correct any entered text in your text box for typos, grammar, and punctuation in a single tap.

  1. Enter text.
  2. If proofreading errors are found, the “Fix it” chip appears on the suggestion bar. Tap Fix it to apply corrections to your text.
    • Optional: To remove the correction, tap Undo.
  3. If more proofreading suggestions are available, tap Fix it More fixes.

Add words to your dictionary

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap an area where you can enter text.
  3. Enter the word you want to add.
  4. Tap the word underlined in red.
  5. Tap Add to dictionary.

Tip: Misspelled words might be corrected as you type. To undo any corrections that may have been made automatically, tap Backspace .

Change the types of suggestions you get

You can choose the types of suggestions you see, like next words or emojis.

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text.
  3. At the top of your keyboard, tap Open features menu .
  4. Tap More Settings Text correction.
  5. Pick from the options.

Turn on Smart Compose suggestions (US only, English only)

You can turn on inline suggestions to make sentences easier to complete and reduce typos.

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap an area where you can enter text.
  3. At the top of your keyboard, tap Open features menu .
  4. Tap More Settings Text correction.
  5. In the “Suggestions” section, turn on Smart Compose.

Smart Compose is available on these messaging apps:

  • Android Messages
  • Google Hangouts and Chat
  • Facebook Messenger
  • LINE
  • Slack
  • Telegram
  • Verizon Messages
  • WhatsApp

Android iPhone & iPad

Handwrite on your keyboard

You can handwrite words on your keyboard to enter text.

Important: Handwriting is not available in all languages.

Turn on Handwriting

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type in, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text. Your keyboard will appear at the bottom of the screen.
  3. At the top of your keyboard, tap Settings .
  4. Tap Languages the language you want to use.
  5. Swipe right and turn on the Handwriting layout. If you don’t find it, Handwriting is not available for your language.
  6. Tap Done.

Select a Handwriting keyboard

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type in, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text. Your keyboard will appear at the bottom of the screen.
  3. Touch and hold Globe .
  4. Select a handwriting keyboard, like English (US) Handwriting. Your keyboard will become a blank writing area where you can enter words.
  5. With a finger or stylus, handwrite words on the keyboard to enter text.

Tip: In most languages, Gboard predicts when you need a space. If it misses one, tap the Spacebar at the bottom of your screen.

Android iPhone & iPad

How to send feedback to Gboard

If you use an Android device, you can send feedback directly from Gboard or through Android Settings.

Send feedback through comma on Gboard

  1. On your Android device, open any app where you can enter text, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. At the bottom left of your keyboard, touch and hold the comma, then move your finger to access Settings .
  3. At the bottom, tap Help & feedback Send feedback.

Send feedback through Android Settings

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open Settings .
  2. Tap System Languages & input.
  3. In the top right corner, tap Help .
  4. At the bottom of the page, tap Send feedback.

Search Google & send results from your keyboard

You can search and share anything from your mobile device, like nearby restaurants, videos, or weather forecasts.

Important: If your device uses Android 8 (Go edition), some of these steps might not work.

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, install Gboard.
  2. Open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  3. Tap where you can enter text.
  4. At the top of your keyboard, tap Open features menu .
  5. Tap Search .
  6. In the search bar, type your request.
  7. At the bottom, tap Search .
  8. Below or next to a search result, tap Share. A link to the page will show in the message field.

Tip: If suggestions show below the search result, you can tap one to see related information.

Android iPhone & iPad

Set up Gboard

After you install Gboard, you can change your keyboard settings and choose your languages.

Download Gboard

  • On your Android phone or tablet, install Gboard.
  • On some Android devices, Gboard is already the default keyboard. To make sure that your device has the most recent version, check for updates.

Important: If your device uses Android 8 (Go edition), some of these steps might not work.

Set keyboard options

Change your settings

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text.
  3. At the top left of the keyboard, tap Open features menu .
  4. Tap More Settings .
  5. Choose which settings to turn on, like Glide typing, Text correction, and Voice typing.

Add Google Search button

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text.
  3. At the top left of the keyboard, tap Open features menu .
  4. Tap More Settings .
  5. Tap Search.
  6. Turn on Show “Search and more” button.

Choose languages & layouts

  1. On your Android phone or tablet, open any app that you can type with, like Gmail or Keep.
  2. Tap where you can enter text.
  3. At the top left of the keyboard, tap Open features menu .
  4. Tap More Settings Languages.
  5. Choose the languages you want.
  6. Select the layout you want to use.
  7. Tap Done.
