RCS chats by Google FAQ

What are RCS chats?

Rich Communication Services (RCS) chats provide an upgraded, rich messaging experience. RCS chats:

  • Show you when someone is typing.
  • Offer read receipts, which show when someone has read or received your message. Read receipts also show your contact when you read their message.
  • Send messages over mobile data and Wi-Fi.
  • Let you share files and high-resolution photos.

When you use RCS chats, your messages are sent with the Rich Communication Services (RCS) protocol over Wi-Fi and mobile data. RCS chats will be turned on only when all the participants in a conversation have RCS. RCS chats are provided by Google or your mobile carrier.

What devices work with RCS chats?

Rich Communication Services (RCS) are available on Android devices and other devices where RCS is turned on in settings. Check your carrier and device settings. Availability of RCS varies by region and carrier.

What happens if I don’t have data, or the recipient isn’t online?

Google Messages can still be sent as SMS or MMS.

You can check and set your default option when RCS isn’t available:

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. At the top right, tap your profile photo or icon Messages settings RCS chats.
  3. Turn Automatically resend as text (SMS/MMS) on or off.

What if RCS chats aren’t available for my device?

To check your RCS availability and status:

  • Tap on your profile photo or icon Messages settings RCS chats.

Tip: If you get the message “Not supported - RCS chats are not supported by your carrier,” RCS isn’t currently supported by your carrier.

To troubleshoot your RCS chats connection:

  1. Update Google Messages from Play Store.
  2. Make sure Google Messages is set as your default SMS app.
  3. If your device has dual SIM slots, and both SIMs are inserted, make sure your Call SIM is configured as your Data SIM:
    1. On your Android device, open your Settings.
    2. Tap Network & Internet.
    3. Make sure your Call SIM is configured as Data.

What if my RCS chats status shows that my carrier doesn’t support, or I’m ineligible to receive RCS?

We’re working to bring RCS support to more countries/regions and carriers.

My RCS chats status says “Connecting” or “Trouble connecting. Awaiting retry…”. How do I get RCS chats?

When we’re in the process of verifying your phone number, your RCS chats status displays “Connecting.” If the “Trouble connecting. Awaiting retry…” status remains for more than 30 minutes, it means Google Messages has trouble with your phone number verification.

If “Verify your number” shows:

  1. Tap your Profile picture or Initial Messages settings RCS chats.
  2. Tap Verify your number.
  3. Confirm your phone number when requested.
  4. Google sends an SMS to confirm your phone number.
  5. Make sure you can receive SMS messages.

If “Verify your number” doesn’t show or the steps above don’t help, tap Details Submit feedback.

How do I know if my message was sent?

Google Messages tells you when your message has been sent, received, and read through the icons next to your message:

Important: These icons won’t show on SMS or MMS messages.

  • Timer : Your message is being sent.
  • Single check : Your message has been sent.
  • Double check : Your message has been delivered.
  • Color-filled double check : Your message has been read.

I don’t currently use Google Messages, what happens if I switch my default app to use Google Messages and start to use RCS chats?

You can make Google Messages your default app as described here. You won’t lose any existing SMS/MMS messages if you change your default app to Google Messages and you’ll be able to use Google Messages’ benefits such as Google Messages for Web, Smart Replies, and RCS chats (where supported).

If your previous messaging app supports proprietary features or non-interoperable forms of messaging (not SMS, MMS or interoperable RCS), you won’t be able to use those features after you switch.

Will features like typing indicators and read receipts work when the recipient doesn’t have RCS chats?

No, but standard text messaging via SMS/MMS will still work.

Information we use

To make sure your messages are properly delivered, Google uses information like your phone number, device identifiers, and SIM card number. This data may be stored for about a month to keep you connected to RCS and in cases where you temporarily go offline.

When you turn on RCS chats, and each time you send a message, Google checks your contacts to find out if they can also use RCS chats. These checks may go through Google’s RCS infrastructure and other service providers to reach your contacts.

What is the group chat experience when I include people who don’t have RCS chats?

If all the participants don’t have RCS chats turned on, you still may be able to create SMS/MMS groups.

Know if additional cost apply in RCS chats

When you use RCS chats, your messages are sent over Wi-Fi and mobile data. As long as you’re connected to a Wi-Fi network that you don’t have to pay to use, there’s no additional cost to send and receive messages. If your messages are sent using mobile data, the cost is based on your mobile data plan.

How RCS chats work between Android and iOS

You can now use Rich Communication Service (RCS) chats between Android and iPhones. When you chat with an iPhone user friend, you can:

  • See typing indicators in 1:1 conversations
  • Read receipts in 1:1 conversations
  • Manage group chats
  • Send high-resolution photos and videos

FAQs about RCS messaging between Android and iOS

Country or region availability for RCS on iOS devices

RCS chats may not be available to iPhone users depending on users’ country and carrier. For more information about whether you can use RCS on your iPhone, contact your carrier.

Android texts appear as a green bubble when texting with iPhone users

Apple displays text messages that don’t come from an iPhone user as green bubbles. This is also true for messages from other iPhone users who have iMessage disabled.

RCS chats with iPhone users don’t have end-to-end encryption

Google Messages offers end-to-end encryption for your RCS messages with other Google Messages users. The GSM Association (GSMA) sets Mobile and RCS standards and we are currently working to define security standards cross platform.

RCS chats with businesses

Rich Communication Services (RCS) is a modern messaging protocol that enables more dynamic, interactive, and secure conversations than traditional SMS and MMS. You can receive interactive messages from registered businesses through these capabilities. For example, you can browse and shop from a product catalog directly within the chat.

With RCS chats with businesses, you can:

  • Trust the message is from a legitimate business.
    • Unlike text messages that don’t show verification to end users, the chat experience is clearly branded with the company’s name, logo, and a verification check mark.
  • Receive interactive messages that include photos, videos, audio, or PDF files.
    • You can even find a preview of a link before you tap it.
  • Complete tasks quickly within the chat with the suggested reply and action buttons.
    • This means you don’t have to leave your conversation or open a separate app or website to track an order or check a flight.
  • Preserve your interactions with a business from customer service to order tracking.
    • They can be preserved in the chat thread to make it easy to find past messages.

Tip: Availability of RCS on Android varies by region and carrier.

Turn on RCS to chat with registered businesses

If your phone and carrier can use RCS, the option shows in your advanced settings.

Tip: Availability varies, and carrier charges may apply. Contact your carrier for details.

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Tap your profile photo or icon Google Messages settings.
  3. Tap RCS chats Turn on RCS chats.
  • If you can’t find “RCS chats,” tap Chat features.

If you don’t find this option, it may not be available for your phone or carrier.

Learn about RCS chats with registered businesses

When a business registers to use RCS chats, Google or other third-party providers verify the business’s identity. If the business is verified:

  • It has a verified check mark next to the business’ name.
  • It states “verified” under the business profile details.

When you message a business, they’ll receive a read receipt for each of their messages that you read. Learn more about how to turn off read receipts.

  • Verified RCS chats between businesses and users aren’t end-to-end encrypted.
  • Chats are managed by businesses, messaging solution providers, and carriers.
  • Entities that operate RCS business conversations and, in some cases, carriers, may access message content for delivery and other purposes.
  • To protect against spam and abuse, Google has access only to the message content sent by businesses to users. Messages sent by users to businesses can’t be accessed by Google.
Identify if your RCS chat is with a verified business
  • Verified sender: Next to the business’s name, you can find a verified check mark.
    • This check mark indicates that Google, your mobile carrier, or a third-party provider has confirmed the business’s identity.
  • Branded display: At the top of the conversation, you can find the business’s name and logo.
  • No phone number: In the conversation header, you can find the business’s name and description instead of a phone number.

Use interactive features

When you use RCS chats with businesses, it goes beyond simple text. You can find a variety of interactive features:

Use suggested replies in RCS chats with businesses

To send a quick response to businesses, tap the suggested replies like “Track order,” “Talk to a representative,” or choose between “Yes” or “No.”

Use suggested actions in RCS chats with businesses

  • You can take specific actions like call a business, visit a website, or share location when you use a quick reply button.

  • You can also save or access info from RCS chats with business when you use other apps. If you tap on the Google Wallet link sent from a business, this allows you to add vouchers, boarding passes, or tickets from the business directly to your Google Wallet app.

Use cards & carousels

You may receive and interact with a combination of media, text, and suggestions in one cohesive message all in one message or in multiple cards that they can swipe through.

  • To browse different products or services, you can also swipe through multiple cards in a carousel.

Review feature availability for RCS chats with businesses

Some RCS chat features don’t work or work differently for RCS chats with businesses.

[TABLE]

Get more info about a business

To get a business’s information, tap the business’s name Information.

To review the business’s privacy policy and terms of service:

  1. Tap Info & options Options.
  2. Select an option:
    • View Privacy Policy
    • View Terms of Service

Control your interactions in RCS chats with businesses

You have control over your interactions in RCS chats with businesses. You can stop receiving non-essential messages, like promotions, from businesses in Google Messages. This helps you manage your inbox and focus on messages that matter to you.

To manage unwanted messages and your engagement in Rich Communication Service (RCS) chats with a business, you can:

  • Unsubscribe from unwanted messages: You can choose to unsubscribe from non-essential messages.
    • You can provide a reason for unsubscribing, like:
      • Not signed up
      • Too many messages
      • No longer interested
      • Spam
      • Other
        • You can manually type the reason for unsubscribing.
  • Block and report spam: If you want to go a step beyond unsubscribing from a business, you can block them and report them as spam.

Unsubscribe from a business

If you don’t want to receive non-essential messages from a business such as promotions, you can unsubscribe from an RCS chat with a business.

To unsubscribe:

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open the conversation with the business you want to unsubscribe from.
  3. At the top right, tap More Unsubscribe.
  4. Confirm your choice if prompted.

After you unsubscribe:

  • You should no longer receive non-essential messages from that sender. You may still receive essential, requested messages from them. This includes one-time passwords or transactional messages, like boarding passes.
  • You may receive a confirmation of your unsubscribe request. This confirmation may include information to help you manage your communication preferences.
  • Google Messages doesn’t block future messages. The conversation with the business remains in your inbox.
    • If you report the conversation as spam, it moves to the “Spam & blocked” folder.
  • If a business can’t unsubscribe you directly in the chat, they may send a follow-up message. This message should include a direct link to their website or app where you can manage your communication preferences.

Tips:

  • From the chat menu within a conversation, tap Unsubscribe.
  • For businesses that send promotions or a mix of promotions and other updates like appointment reminders, you might find “Unsubscribe” directly in the chat conversation after a certain number of unread messages.
  • “Unsubscribe” is available in RCS chats with businesses in Brazil, France, Germany, India, Netherlands, Mexico, Spain, UK, and US.

When you unsubscribe, Google Messages sends a “STOP” message from your phone number to the business. It’s the business’s responsibility to honor your request.

  • Country or region (country code): Germany (DE), India (IN), Netherlands (NL), United Kingdom (GB), United States (US); “STOP” message: STOP
  • Country or region (country code): Spain (ES), Mexico (MX); “STOP” message: BAJA
  • Country or region (country code): France (FR); “STOP” message: STOP
  • Country or region (country code): Brazil (BR); “STOP” message: parar

Resubscribe to a business

To receive messages from a business again, you can resubscribe to them.

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open the conversation with the business you want to resubscribe to.
  3. At the top right, tap More Subscribe.
  4. Confirm your choice if prompted.

Tips:

  • The “Subscribe” button might appear at the bottom of the conversation if the user has previously unsubscribed.
    • Alternatively, in the conversation menu or from an in-chat link, tap Subscribe.
  • If you send a message to a business after you unsubscribe, it’s considered a request to resubscribe. This includes all message types like promotions.
  • You can resubscribe to a business outside of Google Messages, for example, on their website. It’s the business’ responsibility to update your subscription status. They must also resume message delivery within RCS.

When you resubscribe, the “START” command reverses a previous opt-out. This allows you to receive the business’s messages again.

  • Country or region (country code): Germany (DE), India (IN), Netherlands (NL), United Kingdom (GB), United States (US); “START” message: START
  • Country or region (country code): Spain (ES), Mexico (MX); “START” message: ALTA
  • Country or region (country code): France (FR); “START” message: Démarrer
  • Country or region (country code): Brazil (BR); “START” message: começar

Block or report business messages

If you no longer want to receive messages from a business, you can block and report.

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open the conversation with the business you want to block.
  3. Below the conversation, tap Block & report.
  4. Alternatively, tap More Block & report spam.
  5. Select an option:
    • Report as spam: To report spam or poor business behavior to Google, tap the checkbox. This will also block the business.
    • Block: Confirm that you want to block the business.

Tips:

  • Once you block a business, the conversation you had with them is moved to the “Spam & blocked” folder.
    • To find business messages that you’ve blocked, tap More Spam & blocked.
  • When you report business messages as spam, the sender’s information and up to the 10 most recent messages sent by the business go to Google and may go to your carrier.
  • Google spam detection and prevention may ephemerally process the contents of messages sent by businesses, and use those signals to train AI models to improve spam detection and prevention.
    • Google doesn’t have access to message content sent by users to businesses.
  • Google employees and contractors may review spam information to help improve Google’s protections against spam and abuse.
  • Human reviewers have restricted and audited access to this information for 30 days. Only the spammer’s identifier is retained for the spam review.

Unblock businesses

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Tap More Spam & blocked.
  3. Tap the name of the business you want to unblock.
  4. To confirm, tap Unblock.

Related resources

  • Turn on RCS chats in Google Messages

Report spam in Google Messages

When you report a conversation as spam, you also block the sender and move the message to your “Spam & blocked” folder. Google employees and contractors may also review your spam information to help improve Google’s spam and abuse protection for Google Messages and Google’s other products and services. Reported conversations are also used to train AI models to improve spam and abuse protection.

When you report spam:

  • The spammer’s phone number is reported to Google.
  • Google gets a copy of the last 10 incoming messages from the spammer so we can improve spam detection. In a group conversation, this can include messages from users other than the spammer:
    • Each reported message includes the sender’s phone number and a timestamp of the message.
    • Each reported message sent with Rich Communication Services (RCS) includes an identifying RCS Message ID.
    • Each reported RCS group conversation includes an RCS Group ID.
    • Each reported message includes the name of the group of conversation.
    • Each reported message includes the profile names and phone numbers of all remote users in the conversation except the user who sent the report.
  • Your country code based on SIM card and IP is reported to Google.
  • Your past replies to the spammer aren’t sent to Google.
  • Your name and phone number aren’t linked to the spammer’s messages.
  • The spammer can’t view your report and won’t know about it.

Your report might create a separate “Spam reporting” conversation. This will send a copy of the spammer’s number plus the most recent text message to your mobile carrier. These conversations may automatically go to the “Spam & blocked” folder.

Sending spam reports is optional. You can also block a phone number and don’t have to report it to Google. Learn more about spam protection and how to block or unblock a number.

When Google Messages detects a message as spam, that message can be dropped and senders can be suspended if found to violate the Google Terms of Service.

Important: If your Google Messages for web syncs with Google Fi, use the Android instructions.

Block & report a conversation

  1. On your computer, open Google Messages for web.
  2. Next to the person you want to block, click More options Block & report spam OK.

Unblock a conversation

  1. On your computer, open Google Messages for web.
  2. In the conversation list, click More options Spam & blocked.
  3. Find the contact in the list and select Unblock Done.

When you remove a spam report

To improve spam classification quality, Google receives information about removed spam flag:

  • Each reported message sent with Rich Communication Services (RCS) includes an identifying RCS Message ID.
  • Each reported RCS group conversation includes an RCS Group ID.
  • The content of the message isn’t shared with Google.

Send & read text & voice messages in Google Messages

You can send and receive text messages with friends and contacts on Google Messages.

Important: Some of these steps only work on Android 6.0 and up. Learn how to change and update your Android version.

Start a conversation

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Tap Start chat.
  3. In “To,” enter the names, phone numbers, or email addresses that you’d like to message. You can also pick from your top contacts or your whole contact list.

Send a message

  1. Tap the message box.
  2. Enter your message. If you’d like to save it as a draft and go back, tap Back .
  3. When you’re done, tap Send .

Tip: Learn how to share contacts in your messages.

Send a voice message

  1. Tap the message box.
  2. Tap the Microphone .
  3. Record your voice message.
    • The voice message is automatically saved as a draft so you can listen to it before you send it.
    • The voice message isn’t sent until you tap Send .
  4. Tap Send .

Read voice message transcripts

Important: If you turn on Live Captions, transcription is available on web. Learn how to turn on Live Captions.

When you receive a voice message, you can choose to listen to it or to read a transcript of the voice message if Live Captions are turned off.

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open the chat where you received the voice message.
  3. At the top of the voice message recording, tap View transcript.

Forward a message

After you open a conversation, you can send it to a new contact at any time.

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open a chat.
  3. Tap and hold a message.
  4. Tap More Forward.
  5. Choose your contact.
  6. Tap Send .

Read text messages

To read a message that you just got, swipe down from the top of your screen and tap New Message .

You can also open any conversation in Google Messages to read it again.

Mark messages as read & unread
  • Mark all messages as read: Tap More ** Mark all as read**.
  • Mark a message as unread:
    1. In the conversation history, touch and hold the conversation you want to mark as unread.
    2. At the top, tap Mark as unread.
Play a video or recording
  1. To play a video or recording that you received, tap a conversation.
  2. Next to the video or recording, tap Play .
Call someone while in Google Messages
  1. To call someone, tap a conversation.

Read archived messages

Send photos, videos, files, or GIFs

Send voice messages

Share your real-time location in Google Messages

You can share your real-time location directly from Google Messages. This feature allows your friends and family to know your location for the duration of your choice. You can choose:

  • For 1 hour
  • Today only
  • Until you turn this off
  • Custom duration

This provides peace of mind or helps you coordinate meetups easily.

Share your real-time location from Google Messages

To share your location in a chat:

  1. Open the Google Messages app .
  2. To share your location, open a conversation with the person or group you want to share it with.
  3. Tap Attachment Real-time location .
    • To confirm the updates to your Google Location Sharing settings, tap I accept. This is only applicable when sharing the location for the first time.
  4. Choose the duration of the share you want to start from either:
    • For 1 hour: Your location will be shared for an hour from the moment you start sharing.
    • Today only: Your location will be shared until the end of the current day.
    • Until you turn this off: Your location will be shared indefinitely until you manually stop sharing.
    • Custom duration: You can set a specific time period for sharing. The duration can’t last more than 24 hours.
  5. Tap Send .

To share your location with someone who has already shared their location with you:

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. To share your location, open a conversation with the person or group you want to share it with.
  3. Tap the message with your contact’s location.
  4. Next to your name, tap Share.
  5. At the bottom, set how long you want to share your location.
    • For 1 hour: Your location will be shared for an hour from the moment you start sharing.
    • Today only: Your location will be shared until the end of the current day.
    • Until you turn this off: Your location will be shared indefinitely until you manually stop sharing.
    • Custom duration: You can set a specific time period for sharing.
  6. Tap Send .

Tip: You must be signed in to your Google Account to use this feature. If you aren’t, you’ll be prompted to sign in.

Stop sharing your real-time location

To stop sharing your location with someone who has shared their location with you:

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open a conversation with the person or group you’ve shared your location with.
  3. Tap the message with your location.
  4. Next to your name, tap Stop Stop sharing.

Encryption & real-time location sharing

While end-to-end encrypted messages can only be read by people in your chat, Google Find Hub location sharing is powered by Maps and processes your location to provide the location sharing feature and is subject to Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Learn more about location sharing.

Troubleshoot RCS chats with businesses

You can troubleshoot issues with your RCS chats with business like starting a business chat or finding other ways to contact a business.

Important: To control which businesses send you RCS messages, you can unsubscribe or resubscribe to RCS chats with businesses. Learn about your RCS chats with businesses.

Troubleshoot RCS chats with businesses

Can’t reply to or start a business chat

If you can’t start a chat, an issue may have occurred with a link, QR code, or button. Once you start a chat, you may not be able to reply.

If a business chat is unavailable, make sure:

  • You have RCS chats turned on in Google Messages. Learn how to turn on RCS chats.
  • RCS chats with businesses are supported by your carrier.
  • The business is available in your country or region.

Can’t find RCS chats with businesses on Google Messages for web

Currently, RCS chats with businesses are only available in the Google Messages app.

Can’t find businesses you started an RCS chat with in your contacts

Businesses aren’t automatically added to your contact list after you start a chat with them. You can manually add a business as a new contact.

Other ways to contact the business

If troubleshooting doesn’t resolve the issue, you can find the business’s contact info through the RCS chat.

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Go to the RCS chat with the business you want to contact.
  3. At the top of the chat, tap the business’s name and logo.
    • Alternatively, tap Menu Info & options.
  4. To contact the business directly, use the provided phone number, email, or website.

Turn on RCS chats in Google Messages

With Rich Communication Services or RCS, a modern industry standard for messaging, you can have a more dynamic and secure conversation with someone than SMS or MMS. Learn about Rich Communication Services messaging.

Turn on RCS chats for the first time

When RCS chats are turned on, you can send messages over Wi-Fi and use other features.

If your carrier and device aren’t automatically set up for RCS chats or you can’t turn on RCS chats, learn how to troubleshoot.

Turn RCS chats on or off

Important: It’s not advised to turn RCS chats on and off. If you do, you’ll be removed from group chats. Apply the steps below if you:

  • Swap to a device without RCS and don’t receive messages on your new phone.
  • Switch to another message app and don’t receive your messages.
  • Lose or break your phone but still have your phone number.

If you have access to your device:

  1. On your device, open Google Messages .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial Messages settings RCS chats.
  3. Turn RCS chats on or off.

Tip: If you can’t use your device, use the Google Messages deactivation web portal to turn off RCS chats temporarily.

Understand RCS chat status

To find your status, go to Settings RCS chats.

The possible statuses are:

  • Connected: You can use RCS chats with other people who have them turned on.
  • Connecting: Your phone number is under verification. Please wait.
  • Trouble connecting. Awaiting retry: There’s an issue with your phone number verification. Please wait.
    • If this takes more than 30 minutes, tap Details Submit feedback.
  • Not supported: You can’t use RCS chats. Check your internet connection.

If the message “RCS chats are disabled by your carrier” shows, contact your carrier.

Turn specific features in RCS chats on or off

Let others know you’ve read their messages

To turn on read receipts:

  1. On your device, open Google Messages .
  2. Tap your profile picture or icon Messages settings.
  3. Tap RCS chats.
    • If you can’t find “RCS chats,” tap Chat features.
  4. Tap Send read receipts.

To find out when others have read your message, they must turn on read receipts in Settings.

Show others when you’re typing in a conversation with them

To turn on typing indicators:

  1. On your device, open Google Messages .
  2. Tap your profile picture or icon Messages settings.
  3. Tap RCS chats.
    • If you can’t find “RCS chats,” tap Chat features.
  4. Tap Show typing indicators.

If sending a message doesn’t work, choose how to resend it

If you tried unsuccessfully to send a message over Wi-Fi or mobile data, you can choose how to resend a message:

  1. On your device, open Google Messages .
  2. Tap your Profile picture or Initial Messages settings.
  3. Tap RCS chats.
    • If you can’t find “RCS chats,” tap Chat features.
  4. Tap Resend messages.
  5. Choose how to resend a message.
    • Important: If you choose the option to send as “SMS with a link,” your media could be accessible by a public link not controlled by Google.

Find out if your message is sent by mobile data, SMS, or MMS

The Send icon in the compose bar displays the method your message will be sent. These are the possible ways your messages will send:

  • Send by Wi-Fi or mobile data
  • Send by SMS
  • Send by MMS

Understand sensitive content warnings in Google Messages

To prevent seeing images that contain nudity when you receive, send, or forward messages in Google Messages, turn on the sensitive content warnings feature.

The sensitive content warnings can:

  • Detect and blur images that may contain nudity in Google Messages.
  • Trigger a warning if you try to receive, send, or forward a nude image.
  • Provide resources for you to get help when you receive this type of content.

All detection and blurring of nude images happens on the device. This feature doesn’t send detected nude images to Google.

How sensitive content warnings are triggered

Sensitive content warnings use SafetyCore to perform classification on devices and doesn’t send identifiable data or any of the classified content or results to Google servers. Learn more about SafetyCore.

As a system service, SafetyCore is only active when an application integrates with SafetyCore and specifically requests that content be classified. Images aren’t classified unless they’re sent through Google Messages with the Sensitive Content Warnings feature turned on.

Tip: The sensitive content warnings feature isn’t perfect. It may occasionally detect images that don’t contain nudity or not detect images that contain nudity.

Turn on sensitive content warnings

Important:

  • To use this feature, you need to sign in to your Google Account from Google Messages.
  • For Google supervised users and unsupervised teens, this feature is on by default.
    • Supervised users: This feature can’t be turned off but parents can control it through the Family Link app.
    • Unsupervised teens (13–17 years of age): This feature can be turned off in the Google Account settings.
    • Adults (18+ years of age): This feature is off by default but it can be turned on in Google Messages settings.
  • This feature doesn’t currently work on videos.

For unsupervised teens and adults:

  1. On your Android device, open Google Messages .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial Messages settings.
  3. Scroll to “Protection & safety.”
  4. Tap Protection & safety Manage sensitive content warnings.
    • This redirects you to the Google Account setting “Sensitive content warnings.”
  5. Turn on Warnings in Google Messages.

Learn about sensitive content warnings

When “Warnings in Google Messages” is on, sensitive content warning detects images that contain nudity. If sensitive content warning detects an image that may contain nudity, it blurs the image and displays a warning that offers guidance and resources.

If you decide to check the image you received:

  • To open a helpful resource page, tap Learn why nude images can be harmful.
  • To block the sender’s number, tap Block this number.
  • To open the image, tap Next No, don’t view or Yes, view.
  • To go back to the messages, tap Back.

If you decide to send a nude image:

  • To open a helpful resource page, tap Learn about image sharing and safety.
  • To block the sender’s number, tap Block this number.
  • To send the image, tap Next.
    • To continue, swipe right Yes, send.
    • To cancel, select No, don’t send.
  • To go back to the messages, tap Back.

If you decide to forward a nude image:

  • To open a helpful resource page, tap Learn about image sharing and safety.
  • To forward the image:
    1. Select a recipient.
    2. Tap Next.
  • To go back to the messages, tap Back.

Tips:

  • If you’re not sure what to do, try to talk to or message someone you trust.
  • When you send, receive, and forward an image, you can unblur and blur the image back.
    • To unblur the image: At the bottom right of the image, tap Preview .
    • To blur the image back: At the bottom right of the image, tap Remove preview .

Learn how to troubleshoot

Check why sensitive content warnings don’t work

You can check if you’re logged in to your Google Account from Google Messages.

Understand the basics of privacy in Google Messages

Keeping you safe online means protecting your information and respecting your privacy. That’s why we focus on keeping your information secure, treating it responsibly, and keeping you in control within Google Messages and in every product we make.

Your information is protected by world-class security.

  • For general information about privacy on Google Messages, keep reading this article.
  • For more about privacy tools, visit the Google Safety Center.

Important: To make sure your personal information isn’t shared more widely than you intend, be aware of your Google Account privacy settings. The settings include when messaging people who aren’t in your contacts. Learn how to change your account visibility.

A more secure & helpful experience for you

Your 1:1 and group chat messages with other Google Messages users are private and encrypted end-to-end by default

When you message someone who also has RCS chats turned on in Google Messages, your chat conversations automatically upgrade to end-to-end encryption. With end-to-end encryption, no one can read the content sent between you and the other person.

  • For more information: Use end-to-end encryption in Google Messages
  • For details on how end-to-end encryption works: How end-to-end encryption in Google Messages provides more security
Your contacts

We use information about your contacts to identify if they are available to chat. This makes it easier for you to send messages.

Your location

When you choose to share your location in Google Messages, Google Messages collects your location. To turn off location collection, you can remove location permissions for Google Messages in your device settings.

Google Messages uses data to improve your experience

To improve Google Messages’ performance and reliability, and to help with troubleshooting issues, Google Messages collects performance data, crash logs, and diagnostics. We also use this information to help prevent abuse of our services.

Certain features, like spam detection, require that Google Messages use additional data to improve those features and Google’s other products and services.

  • How Google Messages improves suggestions with federated technology when the “Help improve Messages” setting is turned on
  • Report spam
Google Messages doesn’t use your content for advertising

Google Messages doesn’t use information collected in our app for advertising.

Understanding Google Messages Data Safety

Your security and privacy are important to Google. Your information is only shared with emergency service providers in case of emergency and with your consent.

Location

This data is only collected and shared with your consent when you initiate an emergency messaging session. Two locations are collected:

  • Precise: From your device.
  • Loose: From the satellite.

Both locations are temporarily queued by our server until they are forwarded to the emergency service provider in case of an emergency only.

Personal Information

  • If you initiate satellite emergency text messaging, your name, email address, and phone number are only shared with an emergency service provider.
  • You can choose whether or not to share your emergency messages with your emergency contacts.

Device or other IDs

Your eSim ID number is shared with the Satellite provider so that you can activate the eSIM.

Unsubscribe from business senders in Google Messages

If a business sends you unwanted messages in Google Messages, like promotions and other non-essential content, you can unsubscribe from them.

  • To facilitate the unsubscribe process, Google Messages sends a “STOP” message to the sender from your number.
  • After the “STOP” message is sent, you should no longer receive non-essential messages from that sender.
  • You may still receive essential, requested messages from them after unsubscribing, like one-time passwords or boarding passes requested from that business or confirmation of your unsubscribe request with information to further manage your communication preferences.
  • If a business is unable to comply with your unsubscribe request because you’ve elected to stop receiving messages in your account, the business may instead redirect you to account settings to change your message notifications through your account.

If you want to stop receiving all messages from the sender, you can always block and report them. Learn how to block senders and report spam in Google Messages.

Tips: Unsubscribe is available for:

  • RCS for Business messages in the United States, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Mexico, Spain, and the United Kingdom.
  • SMS or MMS messages in the United States from short codes (phone numbers with 5-6 digits) and alphanumeric senders.

Unsubscribe from a sender

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open the conversation with the business you want to unsubscribe from.
  3. In the conversation menu, tap Unsubscribe.
    • The “Unsubscribe” option might also appear at the bottom of the conversation.
  4. Select why you want to unsubscribe from that sender.
    • For RCS for Business conversations, this information is shared only as aggregated statistics with the carrier and the sender.
    • If you select “Spam,” you get the option to report the sender.
      • Learn how to block senders and report spam in Google Messages.
  5. To unsubscribe from that sender, tap Unsubscribe or Unsubscribe & report.

Tips:

  • To completely block any messages from the sender, from the menu, select “Block & report spam.”
  • To subscribe again, in the conversation with the business, tap Subscribe.

Re-subscribe to a business

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Open the conversation with the business you want to subscribe to again.
  3. In the conversation menu, tap Subscribe.
    • The “Subscribe” option might also appear at the bottom of the conversation.

Update a sent message

You can edit a Rich Communication Services (RCS), SMS, or MMS message after you send it. This feature works:

  • RCS
  • One-on-one conversation with iPhone users who also have RCS chats turned on
  • Group RCS chats even if other participants don’t have editing capabilities

Editing is enabled in the app only, not on the web UI.

The ability to edit a sent message expires after 15 minutes, regardless whether the recipient has read the message or responded to it.

An “Edited” label appears above the message in the conversation for both the sender and recipient.

Edit a sent message

  1. On your device, open Google Messages .
  2. Touch and hold a sent message in a conversation.
  3. At the top of the screen, tap Edit .
    • If you touch and hold a message after 15 minutes, the Edit won’t be available.
  4. Edit the message.
  5. To update the sent message, tap Check .
    • To exit the editing view, next to “Edit message,” tap Exit .

If a recipient doesn’t support the edit feature, they’ll receive a new message marked with a \0.

Use end-to-end encryption in Google Messages

RCS chats between Google Messages users are automatically upgraded to end-to-end encryption. With end-to-end encryption, no one can read the content sent between you and the other person. End-to-end encryption works for both 1:1 chats and groups when all conversation participants use Google Messages with RCS chats turned on.

Check if a conversation is end-to-end encrypted

End-to-end encrypted conversations have:

  • A banner that says ” RCS chat with [contact name or phone number].”
  • A lock on the send button when you compose a message.

If the send button doesn’t have a lock, make sure you and the person you message both have:

  • The latest version of Google Messages.
  • If your device came with the Carrier Services app installed, update to the latest version of the app.
  • RCS chats in Google Messages turned on.

Confirm with Key Verifier

Important: The key verification feature isn’t supported on Android Go devices, tablets, and wearables.

Improved end-to-end encryption security with Key Verifier for Google Messages app. This lets you verify the public keys of your contacts and confirm that you’re communicating with the person you intend to message over Rich Communication Services (RCS).

If both your device and your contact’s device have the specifications below, learn how to use Key Verification.

To use the Android System Key Verifier app, both your device and your contact’s device must:

  • Run Android 10 and up.
    • Learn how to check and update your Android version.
  • Have Google Contacts app version 4.60.
  • Have Google Messages app version android_20250723.00_p0.
  • Have the Android System Key Verifier app.
    • Download Android System Key Verifier from Google Play.

Make sure RCS chats are turned on in Google Messages, as end-to-end encryption isn’t available for SMS or MMS messages. Learn how to turn on RCS chats in Google Messages.

If you don’t qualify for Key Verifier, continue to use verification code for end-to-end encryption and follow the steps below.

Confirm your verification code

Your conversations are encrypted end-to-end with a key that only you and other conversation participants can access. When you ask them if they have the same code you have, you can verify end-to-end encryption for your individual and group conversations.

To verify end-to-end encryption for individual conversations:

  1. Open the Google Messages app .
  2. Open a conversation or create a new message with a contact you want to verify.
    • In the conversation, all participants must have RCS chats turned on. If RCS chats are turned off, end-to-end encryption can’t be verified.
  3. At the top right of the conversation window, tap More Details Verify encryption.

To verify end-to-end encryption for group conversations:

  1. Open the Google Messages app .
  2. Open a group conversation you want to use.
    • In the conversation, all participants must have RCS chats turned on. If RCS chats are turned off, end-to-end encryption can’t be verified.
  3. At the top right of the conversation window, tap More Group details.
  4. Select a conversation participant you want to verify.
  5. Tap More Verify encryption.

Tips:

  • You can call your contact and read your verification code aloud to make sure your codes match.
  • It’s optional to confirm a verification code. Messages will be end-to-end encrypted even if you don’t take this step.

Troubleshoot messages you’re unable to receive or decrypt

Important:

  • End-to-end encryption may not work on certain Android Go phones.
  • End-to-end encrypted messages only work when you communicate with another Google Messages user. If you or your contact change messaging apps or operating software, Google Messages may not immediately detect when a conversation is no longer eligible for end-to-end encryption. Initially, some messages may not appear or they may be delivered in an unreadable, encrypted format.

If you get an unreadable, encrypted message:

  • Update your app to the latest version of Google Messages.
  • If your device came with the Carrier Services app installed, update to the latest version of the app.
  • Ask your contact to resend the message.

If you changed messaging apps and aren’t receiving messages, you may need to turn RCS chats off.

Tip: You can send messages as chats or resend them as SMS/MMS.

Use reactions

Get started with reactions

Important:

Add a reaction

  1. Tap and hold a message.
  2. Choose an emoji reaction.

Tip: On a computer, to add a reaction, hover over a message. Click Reactions Select a reaction.

Change a reaction

Important: You can only change your own reactions.

Remove a reaction

Important: You can only remove your own reactions.

Find out who applied the reaction

In a group chat, anyone can add a reaction to a message. To find out who added a reaction, tap the group of emoji reactions.

Show iPhone reactions as texts

Important: This feature is only available in the U.S. on text messages sent in English.

When an iOS user reacts to a message, an emoji appears under their message. To get their reactions as texts, turn off the emoji reaction.

The emoji feature only applies when an iOS user reacts to text messages, not to images or any other file types.

  1. Open Google Messages .

Use photomoji

Create photomoji to send as a reaction

Use animated emoji

Most of the emoji are animated. You can send an emoji to see it animate in fun, delightful ways. By default, animated emoji are turned on.

Use screen effects

There’s a lot of hidden messages that’ll trigger Screen Effects. You can send messages like “Happy Valentine’s Day” and see it animate, on both your screen and the recipient’s screen.

Disable animated features

Use filters in Google Messages

You can organize your inbox with filters in Google Messages. After you click the search box at the top of the app, filter options are viewable. Filter options can be used for all message types, including text and multimedia messaging, and Rich Communication Services (RCS).

Use Gemini in Google Messages

You can chat with Gemini in the Google Messages app to draft messages, brainstorm ideas, plan events, or simply have a fun conversation.

What you need

  • Your phone’s language set to a supported language.

  • A personal Google Account that you manage on your own.

Start a chat with Gemini in Google Messages

Important: Chats with Gemini aren’t end-to-end encrypted.

  1. On your Android phone, open Google Messages .
  2. Tap the chat with Gemini, or tap Start chat Gemini.
  3. For the first time, follow any on-screen instructions.
  4. Enter your question or prompt.
    • The first time you chat with Gemini, you can explore different conversations. Just tap a suggestion above the message field.

Examples
  • I haven’t reached out to my friend in a while. Help me draft a short message to check in and reconnect.
  • Suggest a 3-course dinner menu that’s impressive but manageable for a novice cook. Dietary restriction: vegetarian.
  • I’m going to a social event where I barely know anyone. Come up with a few interesting conversation starters.

Give feedback on a Gemini response

  1. Touch and hold the response you want to give feedback on.
  2. At the top, tap Good response or Bad response .

Report a legal issue

  1. Touch and hold a response.
  2. Tap More Report legal issue.

Report legal issue

Delete your Gemini chat

Important: In Google Messages, you can only delete your entire Gemini chat. In your Gemini Apps Activity, you can delete specific prompts from your Gemini chat.

In Google Messages

After you complete the steps below, your Gemini chat is deleted from your Gemini Apps Activity and Google Messages.

  1. In Messages, open your chat with Gemini.
  2. At the top, tap More Delete conversation.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions.

In Gemini Apps Activity

After you complete the steps below, your Gemini chat is deleted from your Gemini Apps Activity. It doesn’t delete the chat from Google Messages or any Android backup of your messages. To also delete it from Google Messages, follow the steps to delete the chat from Google Messages.

  1. Go to your Gemini Apps Activity.
  2. Next to a prompt or response in Google Messages, tap Delete activity item .
    • Activity from Google Messages shows a “ Google Messages” label.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Tip: To access your Gemini Apps activity from the Gemini web app, go to gemini.google.com. Then at the top, tap Menu Settings & help Activity.

What happens when you delete your Gemini chats

  • When you delete your Gemini chat in Google Messages or in your Gemini Apps Activity, Gemini can no longer access the chat.
  • When you delete your Gemini chat in Google Messages, it’s also deleted from your Gemini Apps Activity.
    • If the chat still shows in your Gemini Apps Activity or Google Messages on other devices, check the device you used to delete the chat. Make sure it’s connected to the internet and RCS chats are turned on. Learn how to turn on RCS chats.
  • When you delete your Gemini chat in your Gemini Apps Activity, it doesn’t delete it from Google Messages or any Android backup.
    • To also delete it from Google Messages, follow the steps to delete the chat from Google Messages.

Learn about your location data & Gemini in Google Messages

Gemini in Messages doesn’t have access to your precise location. It uses the general area from your IP address or the home or work addresses in your Google Account to give relevant responses to prompts like “What’s the weather?” Learn more about how Gemini in Messages estimates your general area.

Use Mentions in Google Messages

To specifically call attention to participants within an RCS group chat, use Mentions in Google Messages. This feature:

  • Helps recipients easily find and read messages relevant to them.
  • Ensures mentioned persons receive a notification even if their notifications for that specific group chat are muted.

Understand Mention availability

  • The Mentions feature is only available in RCS group chats. This isn’t supported in MMS group chats.
  • To use Mentions, RCS chats must be available and turned on for all group chat members.
    • RCS availability can vary by:
      • Country or region
      • Carrier

Mention someone in an RCS group chat

  1. On your device, open Google Messages .
  2. Find an active RCS group chat.
  3. In the message composition box, type “@” or the name of the contact.
    • If there’s a match in the group, you’ll get suggestions.
  4. From the contact list, select the correct person’s name.
    • After you select a contact, you can edit the displayed text of the mention.
    • Example: If a contact is saved as “My neighbor Frank,” change the mention to simply “Frank” to make it more appropriate or concise.
  5. Enter your message.
  6. Tap Send .

Learn how a mentioned person gets notified

When you mention someone, the mentioned person receives a notification on their device. This happens even if their notifications for that specific group chat are muted. You can also know that you’ve been mentioned easily when you look at the conversation screen, homescreen, or through the conversation list.

Use real-time text (RTT) with calls

Real-time text (RTT) lets you use text to communicate during a phone call. RTT works with TTY and doesn’t require any additional accessories.

Important:

  • The information in this article might not apply to all devices. To find out if you can use RTT with your device and service plan, check with your carrier. RTT uses call minutes, just like a voice call.
  • At this time, Google Fi doesn’t support RTT. Learn more about Google Fi accessibility features.

Step 1: Turn on RTT

To turn on RTT, go to your Phone app settings.

Step 2: Use RTT

You can place a call with RTT, or you can switch from voice to RTT during a call.

Make a call with RTT

Important: This option is available if you chose “Always visible” in your Phone app settings.

  1. Open your device’s Phone app .
  2. Pick who to call:
    • To enter a number, tap Dialpad .
    • To pick a saved contact, tap Contacts .
    • To pick from numbers you’ve recently called, tap Recents .
    • To pick from contacts saved to speed dial, tap Favorites .
  3. Tap RTT . While the phone rings, the other person’s screen displays an invitation to join the RTT call .
  4. After the other person answers, enter a message in the text field. The text that you enter is visible to the other person as you type.
  5. When you’re done with the call, tap End call . If your call is minimized, drag the call bubble to the bottom right of the screen.
Switch from voice to RTT during a call

Important: This option is available if you chose “Always visible” or “Visible during call” in your Phone app settings. You can switch to RTT on any call, whether you started or received the call.

  1. During a call, tap RTT .
  2. Enter a message in the text field. The text that you enter is visible to the other person as you type.
Merge, hold, or switch to voice

These options are available on select carriers.

  • To switch from RTT to a voice call, tap More Switch to voice call.
  • To place the call on hold, tap More Hold.
  • To merge the RTT call with another voice or RTT call, tap More Merge calls.

Tips for using RTT during a call

  • The text that you enter appears to the other person in real time, unlike with chat messaging. For example, if you make a mistake and then delete it, the other person can see the mistake and the deletion.
  • The other person can request to switch to RTT, even if you’ve selected “Not visible” in your Phone app settings.
  • RTT calls include an audio stream. To mute or un-mute your microphone, tap Mute .
  • You can have multiple RTT calls going at the same time.
  • You can use RTT to call emergency services.For select carriers, RTT is available for emergency calls even if you’ve selected “Not visible” in your phone app settings.
  • RTT isn’t available when roaming abroad.

View a call transcript

  1. Open your device’s Phone app .
  2. Tap Recents .
  3. Tap the call Call details.
  4. Tap See transcript.

Delete a call transcript

You can delete a transcript in either of the following ways:

  • Delete the call in your call history. Learn how to delete call history.
  • Clear Phone app data in Android settings. Learn how to clear app data.

Tip: On Google Pixel devices, your call transcript is only stored within the Phone app, and other apps don’t have access to your call transcript. Other devices might work differently. To find out how your transcript is stored, check with your device manufacturer.

  • Start a video call with Google Meet.
  • Share your location.

By default, Suggested actions is turned on in Google Messages, unless you turn it off.

Turn off Suggested actions

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. At the top right, tap More options Suggestions in chat.
  3. Turn off Suggested actions.

Welcome to Google Messages

Google Messages is more than just a messaging app. It’s a richer, safer, and more expressive way to connect.

Understand how Google Messages works

Powered by Rich Communication Services (RCS), Google Messages has revolutionized how you connect:

  • Rich communication:
    • Share high-quality photos and videos.
    • Know when friends type a message.
    • Enjoy dynamic group chats with your iPhone friends with the ability to add, join, or leave.
  • Personal touch: Make conversations unique with features like custom chat bubbles or fun selfie GIFs.
  • Privacy and security: Enjoy the best spam protection out there. Your chats with other Google Messages users are protected with end-to-end encryption.
  • AI-powered messaging: Craft the perfect message with Gemini and other intelligent features.
  • Seamless across devices: Start a chat on your phone and continue it effortlessly on your tablet or computer.

Tip: Availability of RCS varies by region and carrier.

Explore the fun features in Google Messages

Selfie GIFs

To add a fun and creative twist to your conversations, you can create and send short, personalized GIFs directly from your Google Messages chats.

Voice messaging with Voice Moods

Bring your voice messaging to life with Voice Moods. With 9 different emotions to choose from, your voice can sprinkle heart-eye emoji, fume with fireballs, and break out the party popper. The recipient can hear your words along with a visual effect that expresses how you feel at that moment. Thanks to user feedback, we increased the bitrate and sample rate to improve the overall audio quality of voice messages.

Screen Effects

With Screen Effects, your messages come alive with vibrant animations that transform your words into visual displays that dazzle. Simply type specific messages like “It’s snowing” or “I love you” and watch your screen erupt in a symphony of colors and motion. Together, with your friends, try to uncover 15 or more hidden Screen Effects prompt words.

Custom Bubbles

With new Custom Bubbles, you can customize the bubble color and backgrounds of your conversation and the person you communicate with. If you like, pick a different color for every chat. It’s no longer about blue or green. Now, you can differentiate your conversations and avoid accidental text in your family group chat about a weekend update meant for your friend.

Reaction Effects

Reaction Effects is an addition to your messaging experience that injects more life into your conversations. Picture this: Your friend texts you to let you know the 2 of you have reservations in that trendy new restaurant that everyone has been buzzing about. If you react to the message with a simple Thumbs up emoji, magic instantly unfolds as an animated trio of hands dances around the message bubble. The feature, designed to add a dynamic twist to your chats, embraces the power of expression with 10 of these popular emoji: .

Profile

Easily change your profile name and picture that accompanies your phone number. Your self-expression is important so you can now change how you appear across Google. This helps people recognize you, particularly in group chats.

Powered by AI features

  • To draft messages, brainstorm ideas, plan events, or simply have a fun conversation, in the Google Messages app, you can chat with Gemini.
  • To get suggestions to start or reply to a conversation or to rewrite a drafted message in different styles, use Magic Compose.
  • Transform your favorite photos into reactions with the help of on-device Google AI with Photomoji.

Your chats stay private with automatic previews

With automatic previews, Google Messages makes chatting easier and safer. This feature works with your message data while keeping your messages private. And it’s optional — so you’re in control.

How automatic previews work

When you turn on automatic previews, you’ll find preview cards from Google related to certain content in your messages and when you search in the app. Cards appear for links, places, and other types of content that the Google Messages app is able to recognize over time.

How we protect your data

Automatic previews only use select info (like addresses and links) without linking it to identifiers like your name or phone number.

We use only the info needed for a preview

The Google Messages app uses on-device intelligence to automatically spot specific things, like links or street addresses, in your chat history. We use those links and addresses to create preview cards.

We use data without personally identifying you

Those specific things, like links and addresses, are the only parts of your message content that we use in this feature. They’re sent to Google for a quick, secure lookup without saving them to your Google Account or Location History, and without linking them to identifiers like your name or phone number.

You’re in control

You can turn automatic previews on or off at any time in Settings:

  1. Open Google Messages .
  2. Tap your profile photo or icon Settings.
  3. Tap Automatic previews.
  4. Turn Show all previews on or off.

Automatic previews include web link previews, but you can choose to only show web link previews. Learn even more.

Your chats stay private with Gemini in Google Messages

Google Messages can show you suggestions to get more info from Gemini about movies, restaurants, and more. Gemini suggestions let you see and share helpful info quickly, without leaving your conversation.

How suggestions work

Suggestions are:

  • Created by technology that’s built into your device so your conversations stay in the Google Messages app
  • Based on your recent chats
  • Only visible to you, but if the person you’re chatting with uses Google Messages, they might get the same ones

If you tap a suggestion, Google Messages asks Gemini to search for that term. Results show up as a card that you can see and share in your conversation.

If you’re signed in to Gemini, your searches show up in My Activity. Only your search terms are sent to Gemini, not your conversation.

Notes:

  • Gemini can read what’s on your screen if you use an option called “Use screen context.”
  • If you’re signed in to Gemini, it will use that Google Account when you search.
  • To improve suggestions, Google Messages sends Google the category of the suggestion (for example, a movie, weather, or restaurant), and whether you tapped it.

How we protect your data

Your conversations are personal, and that’s why Google Messages uses technology that keeps them private.

Conversations stay in the Google Messages app

The Google Messages app creates suggestions with technology that’s built into your device. This way, your conversations stay in the Google Messages app. They aren’t sent to Gemini or Google servers.

Shared cards don’t identify you

Cards that you share from Gemini don’t have any of your personal information, like your name, email, or when you last visited a place.

Cards you share with people who use Google Messages are saved temporarily on Google servers but aren’t linked to you. If you share a card with someone who uses another app, they’ll see a URL to Google search results.

Suggestions use only regional location

To offer relevant suggestions, Google Messages gets lists of local places for large regions from Google servers. For example, if you’re in Seattle, you might get a suggestion for Pike Place Market.

If Google Messages has location permissions, it can request and download these lists. When Google Messages makes the request, your device’s exact location and any personal identifiers, like your name, email, or phone number, aren’t sent to Google servers.

Important: When you use Gemini, it uses your device’s location settings and the Google Account linked to your Gemini to provide results.

You’re in control

  • To view and delete suggestions you tapped, go to My Activity. If you delete an item there, it won’t be deleted from your chat.
Gemini settings stay separate

When you use Gemini suggestions in Google Messages, these stay the same:

  • How your Google Account works with Gemini
  • Your device’s location settings, which are used by Gemini

About Google Photos features for Pixel devices

Important: If you have backup turned on, your edits will sync to your Google Photos account. To use some features, you must have backup turned on. Learn how to backup photos & videos.

If you’re a Pixel user, Google Photos gives you access to additional features available just on Pixel devices. Pixel users can always use the full range of editing tools on Google Photos. Learn about other editing features.

Use Google Photos features available just on Pixel devices

Best Take

Important: This feature is available on Pixel 8 and later.

If someone blinks or looks away in your group photos, Best Take blends similar photos into one photo where everyone looks their best. You can choose your favorite facial expressions and create your own Best Take.

To edit a photo using Best Take:

  1. Open the Google Photos app .
  2. Open a photo from a sequence of similar photos that includes one or more people.
  3. At the bottom, tap Edit Actions Best Take.
    • Alternatively, you might need to tap Edit Tools Actions.
    • You can scroll through the categories at the bottom to find “Best Take.“
  4. Tap on a face bubble to choose a different expression.
  5. When you’re satisfied, tap Done .

Audio Magic Eraser

Important: This feature isn’t available on tablets. It’s only available on Pixel 8 and later.

To reduce unwanted sounds or to turn up sounds from videos, you can use Audio Magic Eraser on your Pixel phone.

  1. On your Pixel phone, open the Google Photos app .
  2. Tap on the video you want to edit.
  3. At the bottom, tap Edit Audio Audio Eraser.
    • To have your phone automatically adjust the video for you: Tap Auto.
    • To manually adjust sounds:
      1. Tap a sound.
      2. Adjust the slider.
    • To adjust the volume of different speakers: Adjust the slider for each speaker.
  4. At the bottom right, tap Save copy.

Tips:

  • Before you save a video, you can test what it sounds like. On the video thumbnail, tap Play .
  • Sound options depend on your video. Not all options are available at the same time.

Zoom Enhance

Important:

  • This feature is only available on Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold.
  • This feature isn’t available for images with resolution higher than 12.5 MP.

Zoom in on an existing photo to make the image more crisp and detailed.

  1. On your Pixel device, open the Google Photos app .
  2. Select the photo you want to edit.
  3. At the bottom, tap Edit Actions Zoom Enhance.
    • Alternatively, you might need to tap Edit photo Tools Zoom Enhance.
    • You can scroll through the options to find “Zoom Enhance.”
  4. Pinch out with 2 fingers to zoom in on a certain part of the photo that you’d like enhanced.
  5. Tap Crop and enhance.
    • You can also use this feature without cropping your photo first. Just simply tap Enhance details.
  6. To keep the enhanced photo, tap Save as copy.

Tip: To compare the enhanced and original images, tap and hold the photo.

Tip: Learn how to make edits just by asking in Google Photos.

Pixel Camera features which require Google Photos

Some features in the Pixel Camera app require Google Photos.

Auto Best Take

Important: This feature is only available on Pixel 10 devices.

Auto Best Take requires both Pixel Camera and Google Photos. For group photos of 2 or more faces, with a single shutter tap, Pixel Camera may intelligently capture a burst of high-quality HDR+ images. Google Photos may also automatically create a new Best Take by merging everyone’s best facial expressions into a new image, where everyone looks their best.

To use Auto Best Take, turn on Top Shot and Auto Best Take in Camera settings. Learn how to get great photo with Top Shot and Auto Best Take.

Video Boost

You can capture videos on your Pixel camera with better lighting, colors, and details. Video Boost also enables Night Sight Video. To use Video Boost, the video must be backed up in Google Photos. Learn how to use Video Boost on your Pixel phone.

About premium print series

You can have 10 photos printed on 4x6 inch card stock and sent to you every month. Photos are selected based on photo attributes and preferences, and you have the control to edit and swap photos before they ship, or skip a month.

Important:

  • Prints are only shipped within the US and take 10 to 14 business days under Economy shipping. Shipments can be tracked through UPS until they are transferred to your local post office for delivery. The shipping cost on all orders is included in the subscription cost and can’t be changed or expedited. Tax isn’t included.
  • Some features aren’t available in all states.

How monthly selection works

When you sign up, you can set your preferences and choose how to customize your prints. Each month, we’ll automatically email you a link with 10 photos to review and edit, if you’d like.

Important: You have 5 days to replace or edit the photos we select for you. If you don’t make any changes to your suggestions, these prints will be included in your order. During the 5-day review period, an authorization charge is temporarily applied to your payment method. After your prints are shipped, the monthly charge will be applied.

After the review period, we’ll send another email to confirm that the photos have been printed.

How your photos are selected

Based on your preferences, 10 of your photographs from your Google Photos account are automatically selected. We also use photo categories such as the ones below to make the selection:

  • Favorite photos
  • Recently edited photos
  • Upload time
  • Resolution quality
  • Duplicate photos
  • Featured people and pets (not available for all users)

How to customize your prints

Important: Once you receive your monthly selection email, you have 5 days to change your selected photos.

There are several ways to customize your prints.

  • Paper finish: Select matte or glossy paper finish options.
  • Print border: Choose whether to have a one-eighth inch (3.175 millimeters) Border around all of your monthly prints or select No border.
  • Back of print: Add the date on the back of your prints and/or make each print a postcard.

Customize your selected photos from your computer:

  1. Open Google Photos.
  2. Select Print store Premium print series.
  3. At the bottom of the page, under Subscription Settings, select the option you would like to customize:
    • Print options
    • Featured people
    • Shipping and payment

Review or change selected photos

Important: Once you receive your monthly selection email, you have 5 days to change your selected photos.

  1. Review your selected photos.
    • From your notification email, click Review photos.
    • From your browser:
      1. Open Google Photos.
      2. Click Print store .
      3. At the bottom of the page, select Premium print series.
      4. Under “Upcoming deliveries,” select Review.
  2. Replace or edit your selected photos.
    • To replace a selection:
      1. Under the photo, click Replace.
      2. From the preview screen, click on the replacement photo.
    • To edit a selection, under the photo, click Edit .
  3. In the review screen, after you’ve made any replacements or edits, click Save.

Cancel your premium print series

Important: If you cancel on the last day of the review window or after your review window has ended, you will be charged for that month. For example, if your review window starts on the 15th and ends on the 20th, you have until the 19th to cancel and not be charged. If you cancel on the 20th, the cancellation will take effect the next month.

You can cancel your premium print series at any time.

  1. On your computer, open Google photos.
  2. Click Print store .
  3. On the bottom, click Premium print series.
  4. Under “Subscription settings,” click Cancel service.
  5. On the confirmation dialog, click Cancel.
  6. Click Cancel premium print series Confirm.

Tip: When you cancel your premium print series, your preferences are deleted. You can sign up again, but you’ll have to reset your preferences.

How to skip a month

Skip a month to pause delivery. If you skip a month, you won’t be charged for that month and prints and payments will resume next month. You can only skip one month at a time, and only during the 5-day review window.

  1. On your computer, open Google Photos.
  2. Click Print store Premium print series.
  3. Under “Subscription settings,” click Cancel service.
  4. On the confirmation dialog, click Cancel.
  5. Select Skip this month Confirm.

Manage your order

Change your shipping address

  • Changes made during or after the 5-day photo review period will go into effect the next month.
  • For the first month’s order, you have two hours after you initially subscribe to make changes to your shipping address.
  1. On your computer, open Google Photos.
  2. Click Print store Premium print series.
  3. Under “Settings” at the bottom of the page, click Shipping & Payment.
  4. To change the shipping address, click Edit.
  5. Update your shipping address.
  6. When you’re satisfied with your updates, click Save.

Report a missing or damaged print

If your print never arrived within the expected delivery window or you received a damaged print, contact us. Damage includes shipping-related damages or any other physical flaws.
