Use Call Notes in Phone app

Important: Call summaries are only available in English.

To make sure that you don’t miss any important information on the call discussion, you can use the Call Notes feature on the Phone app. With Gemini Nano, it automatically:

  • Transcribes your calls
  • Generates summaries of your calls like:
    • Important points
    • Next steps
  • Allows you to easily review them later from your call log

Your call contents are stored on your device and aren’t shared with Google.

Check availability for Call Notes

Important: This feature only works on Google Pixel devices, except Pixel A series models.

You can use Call Notes on:

  • Pixel 9 and later devices in:
    • Australia, Canada, Ireland, UK, and the US (in English)
    • Japan (in Japanese)
  • Pixel 10 series devices in: India (in Hindi and English)

Tip: This feature requires a SIM card of the country or region it’s used in.

Get started with Call Notes

To turn on Call Notes:

  1. On your Android device, open the Phone app .
    • Make sure you have the latest version of the Phone app.
  2. At the top right, tap More .
  3. Tap Settings Call Notes.
  4. Turn on Call Notes.
  5. To run, follow the guidance in the Settings.
    • You might need to download additional components required for Call Notes.
  6. After you complete the setup, you can find a button in your in-call UI screen during a call.
    • This allows you to activate Call Notes for the conversation.

To access Call Notes after the first time you use it:

  1. In your in-call UI, tap Call Assist.
  2. To activate the feature, tap Call Notes.

To automatically activate Call Notes for calls:

  1. On your Android device, open the Phone app .
  2. At the top right, tap More Settings.
  3. Tap Call Notes Automatically take Call Notes for calls with these numbers.
  4. Turn on Always take Call notes with selected numbers.
  5. Select a contact to individually add contacts to this list.
    • For non-contacts, tap Call Notes Automatically take Call notes for non-contacts calls.

Troubleshoot Call Notes

Can’t find “Call Notes” menu in settings

Important: To get the feature enabled, avoid clearing storage while you fix Call Notes.

If you’ve met the above conditions and still don’t find the “Call Notes” menu in settings:

  1. Wait for the feature to turn on automatically:
    1. Connect to WiFi and leave your device on and charge it overnight.
    2. If you still don’t find the menu, go to Step 2.
  2. Attempt to manually turn on the feature:
    1. To close and re-open the app, from the bottom, swipe up the Dialer app, hold, then let go.
    2. Re-open the app.
    3. If you still don’t find the menu, go to Step 3.
  3. Reboot the device:
    1. If you still don’t find the menu, go to Step 4.
  4. Submit feedback for the phone team to investigate further:
    1. Force stop the app:
      1. Touch and hold the Phone app .
      2. Tap App info Force stop.
      3. When “Force stop?” dialog shows up, and say “Yes.”
    2. Go to the settings page.
    3. Confirm the “Call Notes” menu isn’t displayed.
    4. File the bug report:
      1. Tap Menu Help & feedback Send feedback.
      2. Tap Account & system information.
      3. Turn on Include system logs.
        • Tip: This step is optional but highly recommended.
      4. Tap Get started.
      5. In the text field, type your issues clearly.
      6. Tap Send .
      7. Attach a screenshot if you have one.
Can’t view Call Notes during calls

If you don’t find “Call Notes” menu on in-call UI, check Settings for any pending actions:

  1. Go to Settings Call Notes.
  2. Check if you have the latest version of the following apps:
    • Phone by Google
    • Speech Recognition & Synthesis by Google
  3. Check if there are pending onboarding steps. If it shows:
    • “Install the latest version of AICore to use this feature:”
      1. Tap the message.
      2. Update in the Google Play Store.
    • “Download the AICore model to use this feature:”
      1. Tap it to download.
      2. Wait for completion.
    • “Install the latest version of Private Compute Services to use this feature:”
      1. Tap the message.
      2. Update in the Google Play Store.
    • “Need to update Google app:”
      1. To update in the Google Play Store, tap Go to Play Store.
    • “Need to download language update:”
      1. Tap Download.
      2. Wait for completion.
    • “Pending audio files download:”
      1. Tap Download.
      2. Wait for completion.

Learn how Call Notes works

Important: Call summaries are only available in English.

When you activate this feature on the call, the participants are notified. The call is transcribed and then summarized by an on-device Gemini model.

After the call ends, you’ll find a brief summary of the key points discussed in the call log next to the call entry. The summary includes:

  • Topics covered: Main ideas and talking points from the call.
  • Dates, times, and places: References to specific dates or times mentioned in the call.
  • Next steps: Any specific next steps or tasks mentioned during the call. Tap on these underlined items to add them to your calendar or reminders app.

Tip: In addition to the summary, you can also access a full transcript and recording of the call for a detailed record of the conversation.

Learn about the benefits of call summary & transcript

  • Improved recall: Easily refresh your memory on what was discussed during a call, even weeks or months later.
  • Enhanced productivity: Quickly identify key takeaways and action items, and add them to your calendar or reminders app so you can stay on top of your tasks.
  • Accessibility: Review call details on the go, even if you weren’t able to take notes during the call.
  • Improved organization: Review your call summaries and transcripts to find specific information quickly.

Learn how to save & manage summaries & transcripts

All your call summaries and transcripts are conveniently saved within the Phone app. You can easily access them through a dedicated section within the app which allows you to:

  • Review summaries: Read through call summaries to get a quick overview of past conversations.
  • Manage storage:
    • To delete an individual Call Note including the call recording, summary, and transcript:
      1. On your Pixel device, open the Phone app .
      2. At the top right, tap More Settings.
      3. Tap Call Notes Delete Call Note.
        • Alternatively, you can remove the call log entry.
    • To delete all Call Notes:
      1. On your Pixel device, open the Phone app .
      2. At the top right, tap More Settings.
      3. Tap Call Notes Delete all Call notes now.
    • To automatically delete Call Notes:
      1. On your Pixel device, open the Phone app .
      2. At the top right, tap More Settings.
      3. Tap Call Notes Automatically delete Call Notes.
      4. Select how long after a Call Note is created for it to be automatically deleted.

Tip: Call Notes may not be available in all languages or regions.

Know that your calls are private

All the calls you make through Call Notes are private to you. Your call recordings, transcript, and summary are private. These are stored on your device and aren’t shared with Google.

Use caller ID & spam protection

When you make or get a call with caller ID and spam protection on, you can get information about callers or businesses outside your contacts or warnings about potential spam callers. With fake call detection, you get alerts if a caller hides their identity or impersonates a contact.

To use caller ID and spam protection, your phone may need to send information about your calls to Google.

If someone outside your contact list calls you, or you call them, that phone number is sent to Google to help identify its business Caller ID name or determine if the call is spam. When you get a call, your phone makes sure it’s from someone on your contact list and not an impersonator.

Google doesn’t get phone numbers from your Contact list. Learn how we help keep your data safe.

Important:

  • Some of these steps only work on Android 6.0 and up.
  • Fake call detection requires:
    • Android 12 or higher. Learn how to check your Android version.
    • The apps Phone by Google, Contacts, and Google Messages are installed.
      • In the Google Messages app, RCS must be turned on.

Turn caller ID & spam protection off or back on

Caller ID and spam protection is on by default. You can choose to turn it off.

To use caller ID and spam protection, your phone may need to send information about your calls to Google. It doesn’t control whether your number shows when you make calls.

  1. On your device, open the Phone app .
  2. Tap More options Settings Caller ID and spam.
  3. Turn See caller ID & spam on or off.
  4. Optional: To block spam calls on your phone, turn on “Filter spam calls.” You don’t get missed call or voicemail notifications, but filtered calls are in your call history, and you can check your voicemail.

Tip: For devices that have an automatic Call Screen feature, there’s no “Filter spam calls” option. Spam autoblocking is one of the automatic Call Screen options. Learn how to screen your calls before you answer them.

  • For Pixel 6 devices and higher: It’s equivalent to the Basic Protection level.
  • For Pixel 5 and lower: It’s equivalent to the “Silently decline” option for the “Spam calls” category.

To change the name on your work or school account, contact your admin.

To change the name or phone number of your business, update your business info.

Turn on Caller ID announcement

To announce a caller’s name or number, turn on Caller ID announcement.

  1. On your device, open the Phone app .
  2. Tap More options Settings Caller ID announcement Announce caller ID.
  3. Choose an option:
    • Always
    • Only when using a headset
    • Never

Mark calls as spam

You can mark all calls from a number as spam to stop getting more calls from them and to report the spammer.

  1. On your device, open the Phone app .
  2. At the bottom, tap Home .
  3. Tap the call you want to report as spam.
  4. Tap Block or Report spam.

Tip: You can tap and hold the call you want to report as spam. Then, tap Block or Report spam.

Recognize spam

If you see “Suspected spam caller” or “Spam” as the caller ID, the call might be spam. You can answer the call, or block and report the number.

Report a mistake in spam protection

If a call from someone you know is marked as spam, you can report the mistake. Future calls to your phone from this number won’t be marked as spam.

  1. On your device, open the Phone app .
  2. Tap Recent calls .
  3. Tap the call mistakenly labeled spam.
  4. To report the mistake, tap Not spam.
  5. To unlock the phone number, tap Unblock .

Verify or share caller ID

You can now share information about businesses you call or call you. That information can:

  • Include a business name or category
  • Be displayed on incoming calls
  • Help others learn more about the business, school, or organization calling

You can verify or suggest a new caller ID.

  1. On your device, open the Phone app .
  2. At the bottom, tap Home .
  3. Tap Was this a business? or Caller ID feedback, then follow the instructions.
  4. Tap Submit.
    • If you verified the phone number isn’t a business number, the information won’t be sent to Google.
    • The information you submit won’t reveal any personal information.

To change your selection after you submit feedback:

  1. In the “Home” tab, touch and hold the call you want to use.
  2. Select Send feedback.

Use Scam Detection

Use Scam Detection to get notified about potential scam calls as they happen. This feature works on your device.

Who can use Scam Detection

Important:

  • Scam Detection only works on Google Pixel devices.
  • Scam Detection only works with a SIM card associated with one of the countries listed below and while the Pixel device is in one of those countries.

The Scam Detection feature is available on:

  • Pixel 6 and later devices in the US.
  • Pixel 9 and later devices in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Spain, and the United Kingdom.
  • Pixel 9a in the US only.

How Scam Detection works

Important: Not all scam calls can be detected. Scam Detection is not 100% accurate and scammers constantly change their tactics. Always use caution when you answer calls from unknown numbers.

Scam Detection is based on the corpus of knowledge about how scammers scam victims.

  • For Pixel 9 and later devices: Scam Detection is powered by Gemini Nano on-device.
  • For earlier devices: Scam Detection uses Google’s on-device machine learning models.

Learn how Scam Detection protects your data

  • The feature is off by default. The user has to actively opt in to turn on the feature. You can always turn off Scam Detection in Settings or from the in-call menu for a particular call.
  • Data processing for Scam Detection is all done on-device. No conversation audio or transcription is stored on the device, sent to Google servers or anywhere else.

Set up Scam Detection on your phone

Important: Make sure you have the latest version of the Phone app. Learn more about how to update your phone app.

To enable Scam Detection:

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Tap More Settings Scam Detection.
  3. Turn on Scam Detection.

Use Scam Detection during calls

Important: To let participants know that the feature is turned on, Scam Detection will have an audible beep at the start of the call and every few minutes after.

  • This feature automatically runs in the background of calls that could be scams. If the likelihood of a scam is high, Scam Detection alerts you with notification, sound, and vibration.

  • To dismiss the alert, tap Not a scam.

  • To end the call, in the notification or at the bottom of the call screen, tap End call.

Turn Scam Detection off

To turn Scam Detection off in a call:

  • At the bottom right of the in-call screen, tap More Scam Detection.

Tip: If you use this method, the feature will be turned off for that particular call only.

To turn Scam Detection off for all calls:

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Tap More Settings Scam Detection.
  3. Turn off Scam Detection.

When you use Scam Detection, you agree to Google Terms of Service.

Use Take a Message for calls you miss or decline

You can use Take a Message at no charge to handle calls you miss or decline. You can find audio recordings of these messages from the “Home” tab of the Phone by Google app. Take a Message can also detect spam among messages left by missed or declined calls from non-contact numbers.

Transcription and peeking

If you’re in a supported country or region, you can get a live transcript of the call as the caller speaks. If you choose to pick up the call, tap Answer. Your notifications show the caller’s name along with the first part of the transcript so you have the idea right away.

Tip: In other countries or regions, only audio is available.

The feature records and transcribes calls directly on your device and doesn’t need a Wi-Fi or mobile data connection. It uses local Speech On-Device API (SODA) to keep privacy and functionality. Calls you answer through Take a Message are treated as “Answered” by your carrier.

Your carrier voicemail handles missed or declined calls when your phone is off or out of network coverage.

Feature availability

As of 2026, you can use Take a Message with live transcription support on Pixel 6 and later phones in these countries or regions:

  • Australia (English)
  • Canada (English and French)
  • France
  • Germany
  • India (Only available in Pixel 10 and later phones, in Hindi (India), and English (India))
  • Ireland
  • Italy
  • Japan
  • Spain
  • United Kingdom
  • United States

In these countries and regions, the service includes audio but doesn’t support transcription features:

  • Austria
  • Belgium
  • Czechia
  • Denmark
  • Estonia
  • Finland
  • Hungary
  • Latvia
  • Lithuania
  • Malaysia
  • Mexico
  • Netherlands
  • Norway
  • Poland
  • Portugal
  • Romania
  • Singapore
  • Slovakia
  • Slovenia
  • Sweden
  • Switzerland
  • Taiwan

Tip: Call Actions like AI-generated next steps only on Pixel 9 and later phones in Australia, Canada, Ireland, United Kingdom, and United States.

Set up Take a Message on your phone

Important: Make sure you have the latest version of the Phone app.

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Tap Menu Settings Take a Message.
  3. Turn on Take a Message.
    • If you’re a non-Visual Voicemail (VVM) user, it might turn on automatically.

Set up Take a Message on your Pixel Watch

Important: To use this on a Pixel Watch, you need a Pixel Watch 2 or later and a Pixel 6 or later phones.

  • Your Pixel Watch must be connected to your Pixel phone over Bluetooth.
  • On your connected phone, you must turn on Take a Message from the Phone by Google app settings.

Use Take a Message

When you miss or decline a call, you get a silent “Taking a Message” notification.

  • Live interaction: You can read the transcript in real-time as the caller leaves their message.
    • Only in supported areas.
  • Join in: To join the call at any time, tap Answer.

Tip: Sometimes Take a Message won’t work, and calls goes to your regular voicemail, if:

  • Your phone is roaming (to avoid international charges).
  • Your phone is off or out of network coverage.
  • The phone rings too long before the feature can start.

Get recordings & transcripts

All calls this feature handles saves an audio recording and a written transcript to your phone.

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Tap Home.
  3. From your call list, select a recent missed or declined call.
  4. Expand the call details to:
    • Play the audio.
    • Find the full transcript.
    • Get AI-generated next steps like “Call Min.”

Learn how Take a Message works

The feature uses content-based detection to identify spam and scams.

  • When a suspicious call is detected, it’s labeled as “Likely scam” or “Spam” in your call log.

Caller’s experience

When you miss or decline a call, Take a Message answers it and plays a greeting for the caller.

  • Custom greetings: Record your own custom greeting up to 60 seconds to replace the default message.
  • Multiple greetings: Record and save multiple greetings and pick which one you want to use.

Troubleshoot: Take a Message

  • Call forwarding: If your carrier’s conditional call forwarding doesn’t work with this feature, turn off Take a Message in the settings.
  • Roaming: To avoid unexpected charges, this feature turns off automatically when you’re roaming.

Use the Phone app to record calls

You can use your Phone app to:

  • Always record calls from unknown numbers.
  • Always record calls from selected contacts.
  • Record an individual call.

Tips:

  • You can playback saved recordings and also modify duration to keep recorded calls.
  • You can see when call recording is active with the call recording indicator.

Important: Only certain devices and carriers support recording calls. Some laws require all people on the call to consent to being recorded. Before the call begins, call participants are notified that the call is recorded.

To record your phone calls:

  • Non-Pixel devices must run Android 9 and up.
  • Pixel devices must be Pixel 6 and up with Android 14 and up.
  • You must have the latest version of the Phone app.
  • You must be in a country or region where call recording is supported. Call recording is widely available, but not in all countries or regions. Features vary based on your country or region.

Turn on “Always record” for unknown numbers

Important: It’s up to you to follow all laws on recording phone conversations. Use call recording responsibly and turn it on only when needed. Automatic call recording and deletion aren’t available in all markets.

  1. On your Android device, open the Phone app .
  2. At the top right, tap More options Settings Call recording.
  3. Under “Always record,” turn on Numbers not in your contacts.
  4. Tap Always record.

Turn on “Always record” for select contacts

Important: It’s up to you to follow all laws on recording phone conversations. Use call recording responsibly and turn it on only when needed. Automatic call recording and deletion aren’t available in all markets.

  1. On your Android device, open the Phone app .
  2. At the top right, tap More options Settings Call recording.
  3. Under “Always record,” tap Selected numbers.
  4. Turn on Always record selected numbers.
  5. At the top right, tap Add .
  6. Choose a contact.
  7. Tap Always record.
  8. (Optional): Repeat these steps for every contact you want to record.

Tip: You can also open a contact to turn on call recording. At the bottom right of the contact card, tap Edit contact Always record calls.

Start a recording from a call

Important: The first time you record a call, you’ll be advised you must comply with local laws related to recording calls. Many jurisdictions require consent by all parties to record the call.

To protect the privacy of all users, when you start recording, both parties are notified with a disclosure that the call is being recorded. When you stop recording, both parties are notified with a disclosure that the call is no longer being recorded.

For non-Pixel devices:

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Make or receive a call.
  3. To record your call, on the ongoing call screen, tap Record .
  4. To stop recording, tap Stop recording .

For Pixel devices:

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Make or receive a call.
  3. To record your call, tap Call Assist Call Recording.
  4. To stop recording, tap Call Assist Stop.
Keep in mind

Important: When a user deletes a call log, the call recording is also deleted.

You can’t record a call in progress:

  • Until the call is answered
  • If the call’s on hold
  • When you create a conference call

Find a recorded call

To keep your recordings private, they’re stored on your device. Calls aren’t saved or backed up off-device.

To find your recording:

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Tap Home** **.
  3. Tap on the caller you recorded.
    • If you recorded the most recent call: Go to the player in the “Home” screen.
    • If you recorded a previous call: Tap History. Then select the recording from the list of calls.
  4. Tap Play .
  5. Optional: To share a recorded call, tap Share .

Tip: You can share recorded calls to supported apps, such as email or messaging apps.

Set how long to keep recorded calls

Important: It’s up to you to follow all laws on recording phone conversations. Use call recording responsibly and turn it on only when needed. Automatic call recording and deletion aren’t available in all markets.

  1. On your Android device, open the Phone app .
  2. At the top right, tap More options Settings Call recording.
  3. Under “Recordings,” tap Delete recordings.
  4. Set how long you want to keep a recorded call before it’s automatically deleted.
  5. Tap Confirm.

Optional: To delete all recordings, tap Delete all recordings now Delete.

Delete a recorded call

Important: It’s up to you to follow all laws on recording phone conversations. Use call recording responsibly and turn it on only when needed. Automatic call recording and deletion aren’t available in all markets.

  1. Open the Phone app .
  2. Tap Home .
  3. Find the number or contact of the recorded call you want to delete.
  4. Tap History.
  5. In the list of calls, find the recording and swipe left.
